source.variation: The cited PRC-order dataset supplies one ordered stroke for 一. Median 1 runs from the left of the square rightward across the middle, rising very slightly before it settles. This learner path adapts those ordered medians to the vendored Noto Sans SC outline while preserving their directions and pen lifts; stroke widths and proportions differ between the Arphic-derived source graphics and Noto Sans SC.

source.citation: Hanzi Writer Data 七.json, ordered stroke paths and medians 1–2 (Hanzi Writer Data snapshot 68d10a4, updated from Make Me a Hanzi, 22 June 2019)
source.variation: The cited PRC-order dataset supplies two ordered strokes for 七. Median 1 crosses from the left edge to the right, rising slightly; median 2 begins high on the right, descends, turns along the foot and lifts into a hook. Two strokes for seven, which is the point the course makes about stroke count and meaning having parted company.

source.citation: Hanzi Writer Data 万.json, ordered stroke paths and medians 1–3 (Hanzi Writer Data snapshot 68d10a4, updated from Make Me a Hanzi, 22 June 2019)
source.variation: The cited PRC-order dataset supplies three ordered strokes for 万. Median 1 draws a long horizontal; median 2 a horizontal from under its middle that turns down and hooks to the left without lifting; median 3 a long left-falling stroke from the top horizontal down to the lower left. Make Me a Hanzi documents that its stroke paths are ordered in proper stroke order, its medians use the same coordinate system for stroke-order animation, and the project follows People's Republic of China stroke order. This learner path adapts those three ordered medians to the vendored Noto Sans SC outline while preserving their order, their directions, the turn, the hook and two intervening pen lifts; stroke widths and proportions differ between the Arphic-derived source graphics and Noto Sans SC.

source.citation: Hanzi Writer Data 上.json, ordered stroke paths and medians 1–3 (Hanzi Writer Data snapshot 68d10a4, updated from Make Me a Hanzi, 22 June 2019)
source.variation: The cited PRC-order dataset supplies three ordered strokes for 上. Median 1 descends the central vertical from the top toward the base. Median 2 separately starts at the vertical and draws the short middle horizontal left-to-right. Median 3 separately draws the long base horizontal left-to-right. Make Me a Hanzi documents proper People's Republic of China stroke order and matching animation medians. This learner path adapts all three medians to Noto Sans SC while preserving their order, both intervening lifts, and the short-before-long horizontal contrast; Noto's vertical is straighter and both horizontals are flatter than the Arphic-derived source graphic.

source.variation: The cited PRC-order dataset supplies four ordered strokes for 不: a top horizontal from left to right, a separately started long falling stroke from the upper centre down-left, a separately started central vertical, and a separately placed right-falling dot. Make Me a Hanzi documents proper People's Republic of China stroke order and matching animation medians. source.variation: The cited PRC-order dataset supplies four ordered strokes for 五. Median 1 is the top bar; median 2 descends from it leaning left; median 3 crosses to the right and turns down; median 4 is the widest stroke and closes the character along the bottom. Make Me a Hanzi documents that its stroke paths are ordered in proper stroke order, its medians use the same coordinate system for stroke-order animation, and the project follows People's Republic of China stroke order. This learner path adapts those ordered medians to the vendored Noto Sans SC outline while preserving their directions and pen lifts; stroke widths and proportions differ between the Arphic-derived source graphics and Noto Sans SC.

source.citation: Hanzi Writer Data 些.json, ordered stroke paths and medians 1–8 (Hanzi Writer Data snapshot 68d10a4, updated from Make Me a Hanzi, 22 June 2019)
source.variation: The cited PRC-order dataset supplies eight ordered strokes for 些, in two pieces. Medians 1–6 draw 此 on top: the middle vertical, a short horizontal to its right, a shorter vertical on the left, a stroke that rises to the right along the foot, then 匕, a short left-falling stroke and a vertical that bends right and hooks up without lifting. Medians 7–8 draw 二 under it as 二 is written alone. Make Me a Hanzi documents that its stroke paths are ordered in proper stroke order, its medians use the same coordinate system for stroke-order animation, and the project follows People's Republic of China stroke order. This learner path adapts those eight ordered medians to the vendored Noto Sans SC outline while preserving their order, their directions, the hook and seven intervening pen lifts; stroke widths and proportions differ between the Arphic-derived source graphics and Noto Sans SC.

source.citation: Hanzi Writer Data 从.json, ordered stroke paths and medians 1–4 (Hanzi Writer Data snapshot 68d10a4, updated from Make Me a Hanzi, 22 June 2019)
source.variation: The cited PRC-order dataset supplies four ordered strokes for 从, in two pieces. Medians 1–2 draw the left 人: a left-falling stroke, then a short right-falling stroke that stops at its middle. Medians 3–4 draw the right 人 as 人 is written alone: a left-falling stroke, then the right-falling stroke. Make Me a Hanzi documents that its stroke paths are ordered in proper stroke order, its medians use the same coordinate system for stroke-order animation, and the project follows People's Republic of China stroke order. This learner path adapts those four ordered medians to the vendored Noto Sans SC outline while preserving their order, their directions and three intervening pen lifts; stroke widths and proportions differ between the Arphic-derived source graphics and Noto Sans SC.

source.citation: Hanzi Writer Data 他.json, ordered stroke paths and medians 1–5 (Hanzi Writer Data snapshot 68d10a4, updated from Make Me a Hanzi, 22 June 2019)
source.variation: The cited PRC-order dataset supplies five ordered strokes for 他, in two pieces. Medians 1–2 draw 亻 on the left: a left-falling stroke, then a vertical restarting under it, as 你 opens. Medians 3–5 draw 也 on the right: a horizontal that rises to the right, turns down and hooks to the left without lifting, a vertical through the middle, then a long vertical that bends right along the foot and hooks up without lifting. Make Me a Hanzi documents that its stroke paths are ordered in proper stroke order, its medians use the same coordinate system for stroke-order animation, and the project follows People's Republic of China stroke order. This learner path adapts those five ordered medians to the vendored Noto Sans SC outline while preserving their order, their directions, the two turns, the two hooks and four intervening pen lifts; stroke widths and proportions differ between the Arphic-derived source graphics and Noto Sans SC. Noto's 也 is wider than the source's, so its turn and hook sit further right.

source.citation: Hanzi Writer Data 价.json, ordered stroke paths and medians 1–6 (Hanzi Writer Data snapshot 68d10a4, updated from Make Me a Hanzi, 22 June 2019)
source.variation: The cited PRC-order dataset supplies six ordered strokes for 价, in three pieces. Medians 1–2 draw 亻 as 他 opens. Medians 3–4 draw 人 spread wide: a long left-falling stroke, then a long right-falling stroke. Medians 5–6 draw a short stroke that drops and falls to the left, then a vertical on the right. Make Me a Hanzi documents that its stroke paths are ordered in proper stroke order, its medians use the same coordinate system for stroke-order animation, and the project follows People's Republic of China stroke order. This learner path adapts those six ordered medians to the vendored Noto Sans SC outline while preserving their order, their directions and five intervening pen lifts; stroke widths and proportions differ between the Arphic-derived source graphics and Noto Sans SC.

source.variation: The cited PRC-order dataset supplies six ordered strokes for 会. Medians 1–2 draw the roof as 今 opens: the left-falling stroke, then the right-falling stroke from a little under the top; medians 3–4 draw two horizontals, the lower one longer; medians 5–6 draw 厶 at the foot as 去 closes: a stroke that falls to the lower left and turns right along the foot without lifting, then a dot. Make Me a Hanzi documents that its stroke paths are ordered in proper stroke order, its medians use the same coordinate system for stroke-order animation, and the project follows People's Republic of China stroke order. This learner path adapts those six ordered medians to the vendored Noto Sans SC outline while preserving their order, their directions, the turn and five intervening pen lifts; stroke widths and proportions differ between the Arphic-derived source graphics and Noto Sans SC.

source.citation: Hanzi Writer Data 体.json, ordered stroke paths and medians 1–7 (Hanzi Writer Data snapshot 68d10a4, updated from Make Me a Hanzi, 22 June 2019)
source.variation: The cited PRC-order dataset supplies seven ordered strokes for 体, in two pieces. Medians 1–2 draw the person piece on the left as 你 opens: a left-falling stroke, then a vertical. Medians 3–7 draw 本 on the right as 本 is written alone: a horizontal, a vertical, a left-falling and a right-falling stroke, then a short horizontal across the vertical near its foot. Make Me a Hanzi documents that its stroke paths are ordered in proper stroke order, its medians use the same coordinate system for stroke-order animation, and the project follows People's Republic of China stroke order. This learner path adapts those seven ordered medians to the vendored Noto Sans SC outline while preserving their order, their directions and six intervening pen lifts; stroke widths and proportions differ between the Arphic-derived source graphics and Noto Sans SC.

source.citation: Hanzi Writer Data 你.json, ordered stroke paths and medians 1–7 (Hanzi Writer Data snapshot 68d10a4, updated from Make Me a Hanzi, 22 June 2019)
source.variation: The cited PRC-order dataset supplies seven ordered strokes for 你. Medians 1–2 draw 亻 first: a left-falling stroke followed by a separately started vertical. Median 3 restarts at the upper right and falls down-left; median 4 restarts below it, crosses rightward, then hooks down-left without lifting; median 5 restarts at the centre, descends, then hooks left without lifting; medians 6–7 separately draw the lower-left dot down-left and the lower-right dot down-right. Make Me a Hanzi documents that its stroke paths are ordered in proper stroke order, its medians use the same coordinate system for stroke-order animation, and the project follows People's Republic of China stroke order. This learner path adapts those seven ordered medians to the vendored Noto Sans SC outline while preserving their directions, both joined hooks, the component order, and six intervening pen lifts; Noto's right horizontal and hooks are squarer than the source medians, and stroke widths and proportions differ between the Arphic-derived source graphics and Noto Sans SC.

source.citation: Hanzi Writer Data 保.json, ordered stroke paths and medians 1–9 (Hanzi Writer Data snapshot 68d10a4, updated from Make Me a Hanzi, 22 June 2019)
source.variation: The cited PRC-order dataset supplies nine ordered strokes for 保, in three pieces. Medians 1–2 draw the person piece as 你 opens. Medians 3–5 draw 口 on the upper right in the order the standalone character uses. Medians 6–9 draw 木 under it: a horizontal, a vertical through it, a left-falling and a right-falling stroke. Make Me a Hanzi documents that its stroke paths are ordered in proper stroke order, its medians use the same coordinate system for stroke-order animation, and the project follows People's Republic of China stroke order. This learner path adapts those nine ordered medians to the vendored Noto Sans SC outline while preserving their order, their directions, the turn and eight intervening pen lifts; stroke widths and proportions differ between the Arphic-derived source graphics and Noto Sans SC.

source.citation: Hanzi Writer Data 信.json, ordered stroke paths and medians 1–9 (Hanzi Writer Data snapshot 68d10a4, updated from Make Me a Hanzi, 22 June 2019)
source.variation: The cited PRC-order dataset supplies nine ordered strokes for 信, in two pieces. Medians 1–2 draw the person piece as 你 opens. Medians 3–9 draw the right side as 警 ends: a dot, a long horizontal and two shorter ones, then 口 in the order the standalone character uses. Make Me a Hanzi documents that its stroke paths are ordered in proper stroke order, its medians use the same coordinate system for stroke-order animation, and the project follows People's Republic of China stroke order. This learner path adapts those nine ordered medians to the vendored Noto Sans SC outline while preserving their order, their directions, the turn and eight intervening pen lifts; stroke widths and proportions differ between the Arphic-derived source graphics and Noto Sans SC.

source.citation: Hanzi Writer Data 候.json, ordered stroke paths and medians 1–10 (Hanzi Writer Data snapshot 68d10a4, updated from Make Me a Hanzi, 22 June 2019)
source.variation: The cited PRC-order dataset supplies ten ordered strokes for 候, in three pieces. Medians 1–2 draw the person piece on the left as 你 opens: a left-falling stroke, then a vertical. Median 3 draws a short vertical beside it. Medians 4–10 draw the right side: a short stroke across the top that turns down to the left without lifting, a horizontal under it, then a short left-falling stroke, a short and a longer horizontal, a long left-falling stroke through the lower one, and a long right-falling stroke. Make Me a Hanzi documents that its stroke paths are ordered in proper stroke order, its medians use the same coordinate system for stroke-order animation, and the project follows People's Republic of China stroke order. This learner path adapts those ten ordered medians to the vendored Noto Sans SC outline while preserving their order, their directions, the turn and nine intervening pen lifts; stroke widths and proportions differ between the Arphic-derived source graphics and Noto Sans SC.

source.citation: Hanzi Writer Data 假.json, ordered stroke paths and medians 1–11 (Hanzi Writer Data snapshot 68d10a4, updated from Make Me a Hanzi, 22 June 2019)
source.variation: The cited PRC-order dataset supplies eleven ordered strokes for 假, in three pieces. Medians 1–2 draw the person piece on the left as 你 opens: a left-falling stroke, then a vertical. Medians 3–7 draw the middle piece: a short horizontal that turns down without lifting, a short horizontal under it, a long vertical down the left side, then two short horizontals against it, the upper one first. Medians 8–11 draw the right piece: a short horizontal that turns down without lifting, a short horizontal under it, a horizontal that turns and sweeps down to the left without lifting, then a long right-falling stroke across it. Make Me a Hanzi documents that its stroke paths are ordered in proper stroke order, its medians use the same coordinate system for stroke-order animation, and the project follows People's Republic of China stroke order. This learner path adapts those eleven ordered medians to the vendored Noto Sans SC outline while preserving their order, their directions, the turns and ten intervening pen lifts; stroke widths and proportions differ between the Arphic-derived source graphics and Noto Sans SC.

source.citation: Hanzi Writer Data 做.json, ordered stroke paths and medians 1–11 (Hanzi Writer Data snapshot 68d10a4, updated from Make Me a Hanzi, 22 June 2019)
source.variation: The cited PRC-order dataset supplies eleven ordered strokes for 做, in three pieces. Medians 1–2 draw 亻 on the left as 你 opens. Medians 3–7 draw 古 in the middle: 十's horizontal and vertical, then 口 under them in the order the standalone character uses. Medians 8–11 draw 攵 on the right: a short left-falling stroke, a horizontal, a long left-falling stroke from the end of the horizontal, then the right-falling stroke across it. Make Me a Hanzi documents that its stroke paths are ordered in proper stroke order, its medians use the same coordinate system for stroke-order animation, and the project follows People's Republic of China stroke order. This learner path adapts those eleven ordered medians to the vendored Noto Sans SC outline while preserving their order, their directions, the turn and ten intervening pen lifts; stroke widths and proportions differ between the Arphic-derived source graphics and Noto Sans SC.

source.citation: Hanzi Writer Data 停.json, ordered stroke paths and medians 1–11 (Hanzi Writer Data snapshot 68d10a4, updated from Make Me a Hanzi, 22 June 2019)
source.variation: The cited PRC-order dataset supplies eleven ordered strokes for 停, in two pieces. Medians 1–2 draw 亻 as 他 opens: a left-falling stroke, then a vertical. Medians 3–11 draw the right side: a dot, a horizontal and 口, as 高 opens; the cover as 写 opens, a short left stroke and a horizontal that hooks down to the left without lifting; then a horizontal and a vertical down the middle that hooks to the left without lifting. Make Me a Hanzi documents that its stroke paths are ordered in proper stroke order, its medians use the same coordinate system for stroke-order animation, and the project follows People's Republic of China stroke order. This learner path adapts those eleven ordered medians to the vendored Noto Sans SC outline while preserving their order, their directions, the turns, the hook and ten intervening pen lifts; stroke widths and proportions differ between the Arphic-derived source graphics and Noto Sans SC.

source.citation: Hanzi Writer Data 偷.json, ordered stroke paths and medians 1–11 (Hanzi Writer Data snapshot 68d10a4, updated from Make Me a Hanzi, 22 June 2019)
source.variation: The cited PRC-order dataset supplies eleven ordered strokes for 偷, in two pieces. Medians 1–2 draw the person piece as 你 opens. Medians 3–11 draw the right side: the roof of 今 (a left-falling and a right-falling stroke), a short horizontal, 月 in the order 月 alone uses, then the knife piece as 到 ends: a short vertical and a long vertical that hooks to the left. Make Me a Hanzi documents that its stroke paths are ordered in proper stroke order, its medians use the same coordinate system for stroke-order animation, and the project follows People's Republic of China stroke order. This learner path adapts those eleven ordered medians to the vendored Noto Sans SC outline while preserving their order, their directions, the turns, the hooks and ten intervening pen lifts; stroke widths and proportions differ between the Arphic-derived source graphics and Noto Sans SC.

source.citation: Hanzi Writer Data 儿.json, ordered stroke paths and medians 1–2 (Hanzi Writer Data snapshot 68d10a4, updated from Make Me a Hanzi, 22 June 2019)
source.variation: The cited PRC-order dataset supplies two ordered strokes for 儿. Median 1 starts near the upper centre and falls down-left; median 2 restarts at the upper right, descends nearly vertically, bends right along the base, then hooks upward without lifting. Make Me a Hanzi documents that its stroke paths are ordered in proper stroke order, its medians use the same coordinate system for stroke-order animation, and the project follows People's Republic of China stroke order. This learner path adapts those two ordered medians to the vendored Noto Sans SC outline while preserving their directions, the second stroke's unbroken bend and hook, and one intervening pen lift; stroke widths and proportions differ between the Arphic-derived source graphics and Noto Sans SC.

Medians 3–4 draw 儿 under it as 儿 is written alone: a left-falling stroke, then a vertical that bends right along the foot and hooks up without lifting. Make Me a Hanzi documents that its stroke paths are ordered in proper stroke order, its medians use the same coordinate system for stroke-order animation, and the project follows People's Republic of China stroke order. This learner path adapts those four ordered medians to the vendored Noto Sans SC outline while preserving their order, their directions, the hook and three intervening pen lifts; stroke widths and proportions differ between the Arphic-derived source graphics and Noto Sans SC.

This learner path adapts those six ordered medians to the vendored Noto Sans SC outline while preserving their order, their directions, the turn, the hook and five intervening pen lifts; stroke widths and proportions differ between the Arphic-derived source graphics and Noto Sans SC.

source.citation: Hanzi Writer Data 光.json, ordered stroke paths and medians 1–6 (Hanzi Writer Data snapshot 68d10a4, updated from Make Me a Hanzi, 22 June 2019)
source.variation: The cited PRC-order dataset supplies six ordered strokes for 光, in three pieces. Medians 1–3 draw the top: a short vertical down the middle, a dot on its left, then a short left-falling stroke on its right. Median 4 draws a long horizontal. Medians 5–6 draw 儿 as 元 ends: a left-falling stroke, then a vertical that bends right along the foot and hooks up without lifting. Make Me a Hanzi documents that its stroke paths are ordered in proper stroke order, its medians use the same coordinate system for stroke-order animation, and the project follows People's Republic of China stroke order. This learner path adapts those six ordered medians to the vendored Noto Sans SC outline while preserving their order, their directions, the hook and five intervening pen lifts; stroke widths and proportions differ between the Arphic-derived source graphics and Noto Sans SC.

Medians 3–6 draw 王 under it as 王 is written alone: two horizontals, a vertical down through them, then the long horizontal along the foot. Make Me a Hanzi documents that its stroke paths are ordered in proper stroke order, its medians use the same coordinate system for stroke-order animation, and the project follows People's Republic of China stroke order. This learner path adapts those six ordered medians to the vendored Noto Sans SC outline while preserving their order, their directions and five intervening pen lifts; stroke widths and proportions differ between the Arphic-derived source graphics and Noto Sans SC.

source.citation: Hanzi Writer Data 公.json, ordered stroke paths and medians 1–4 (Hanzi Writer Data snapshot 68d10a4, updated from Make Me a Hanzi, 22 June 2019)
source.variation: The cited PRC-order dataset supplies four ordered strokes for 公, in two pieces. Medians 1–2 draw 八 on top: a left-falling, then a right-falling stroke. Medians 3–4 draw the piece under it as 能 opens: a stroke that falls to the left and turns right without lifting, then a dot. Make Me a Hanzi documents that its stroke paths are ordered in proper stroke order, its medians use the same coordinate system for stroke-order animation, and the project follows People's Republic of China stroke order. This learner path adapts those four ordered medians to the vendored Noto Sans SC outline while preserving their order, their directions, the turn and three intervening pen lifts; stroke widths and proportions differ between the Arphic-derived source graphics and Noto Sans SC.

source.citation: Hanzi Writer Data 六.json, ordered stroke paths and medians 1–4 (Hanzi Writer Data snapshot 68d10a4, updated from Make Me a Hanzi, 22 June 2019)
source.variation: The cited PRC-order dataset supplies four ordered strokes for 六. Median 1 is the short top dot, descending to the right; median 2 is the long horizontal that spans the character beneath it; medians 3 and 4 are the two legs, the left one falling to the lower left and the right one falling to the lower right. Top before bottom and left before right, the two rules this course has already used for 三 and 八.

source.citation: Hanzi Writer Data 关.json, ordered stroke paths and medians 1–6 (Hanzi Writer Data snapshot 68d10a4, updated from Make Me a Hanzi, 22 June 2019)
source.variation: The cited PRC-order dataset supplies six ordered strokes for 关, in two pieces. Medians 1–2 draw the two short strokes on top: a dot on the left, then a short left-falling stroke on the right. Medians 3–6 draw 天 under them: two horizontals, the shorter one first, a left-falling stroke through them, then a right-falling stroke. Make Me a Hanzi documents that its stroke paths are ordered in proper stroke order, its medians use the same coordinate system for stroke-order animation, and the project follows People's Republic of China stroke order. This learner path adapts those six ordered medians to the vendored Noto Sans SC outline while preserving their order, their directions and five intervening pen lifts; stroke widths and proportions differ between the Arphic-derived source graphics and Noto Sans SC.

source.variation: The cited PRC-order dataset supplies six ordered strokes for 兴, in three pieces. Medians 1–3 draw the top: two dots falling to the right, then a short left-falling stroke on the right. Median 4 draws a long horizontal. Medians 5–6 draw 八 as 只 ends: a left-falling stroke, then a dot. Make Me a Hanzi documents that its stroke paths are ordered in proper stroke order, its medians use the same coordinate system for stroke-order animation, and the project follows People's Republic of China stroke order. This learner path adapts those six ordered medians to the vendored Noto Sans SC outline while preserving their order, their directions and five intervening pen lifts; stroke widths and proportions differ between the Arphic-derived source graphics and Noto Sans SC.

source.citation: Hanzi Writer Data 再.json, ordered stroke paths and medians 1–6 (Hanzi Writer Data snapshot 68d10a4, updated from Make Me a Hanzi, 22 June 2019)
source.variation: The cited PRC-order dataset supplies six ordered strokes for 再. Median 1 draws the top horizontal left-to-right. Median 2 separately descends the left side. Median 3 restarts at the upper left, crosses the frame's top, turns down the right side, then hooks left at the base without lifting. Median 4 descends the central vertical, median 5 draws the inner horizontal, and median 6 closes with the long bottom horizontal left-to-right. Make Me a Hanzi documents proper People's Republic of China stroke order and matching animation medians. This learner path adapts all six medians to Noto Sans SC while preserving their order, both turns inside the enclosing third stroke, the close-last rule, and five intervening lifts; Noto's frame is squarer and its bottom horizontal is flatter than the Arphic-derived source graphic.

source.citation: Hanzi Writer Data 写.json, ordered stroke paths and medians 1–5 (Hanzi Writer Data snapshot 68d10a4, updated from Make Me a Hanzi, 22 June 2019)
source.variation: The cited PRC-order dataset supplies five ordered strokes for 写, in two pieces. Medians 1–2 draw the cover: a short stroke on the left, then a horizontal that hooks down to the left without lifting. Medians 3–5 draw under it a short horizontal, a stroke from under the cover that goes down, right, down again and hooks to the left without lifting, as 号 ends, then a long horizontal along the foot. Make Me a Hanzi documents that its stroke paths are ordered in proper stroke order, its medians use the same coordinate system for stroke-order animation, and the project follows People's Republic of China stroke order. This learner path adapts those five ordered medians to the vendored Noto Sans SC outline while preserving their order, their directions, the turns, the hooks and four intervening pen lifts; stroke widths and proportions differ between the Arphic-derived source graphics and Noto Sans SC. Noto's cover turns straight down at its right end, where the source's hooks to the left.

Medians 3–7 draw the right side: the roof of 今 (a left-falling, then a right-falling stroke), a dot under it, a horizontal that turns and falls to the left without lifting, then a dot at the foot. Make Me a Hanzi documents that its stroke paths are ordered in proper stroke order, its medians use the same coordinate system for stroke-order animation, and the project follows People's Republic of China stroke order. This learner path adapts those seven ordered medians to the vendored Noto Sans SC outline while preserving their order, their directions, the turn and six intervening pen lifts; stroke widths and proportions differ between the Arphic-derived source graphics and Noto Sans SC.

source.citation: Hanzi Writer Data 准.json, ordered stroke paths and medians 1–10 (Hanzi Writer Data snapshot 68d10a4, updated from Make Me a Hanzi, 22 June 2019)
source.variation: The cited PRC-order dataset supplies ten ordered strokes for 准, in two pieces. Medians 1–2 draw the ice piece as 冷 opens: a dot, then a stroke rising to the right. Medians 3–10 draw the right side: a left-falling stroke, a long vertical down the left, a dot at the top right, three short horizontals, a vertical down through them, then a long horizontal at the foot. Make Me a Hanzi documents that its stroke paths are ordered in proper stroke order, its medians use the same coordinate system for stroke-order animation, and the project follows People's Republic of China stroke order. This learner path adapts those ten ordered medians to the vendored Noto Sans SC outline while preserving their order, their directions and nine intervening pen lifts; stroke widths and proportions differ between the Arphic-derived source graphics and Noto Sans SC.

source.citation: Hanzi Writer Data 力.json, ordered stroke paths and medians 1–2 (Hanzi Writer Data snapshot 68d10a4, updated from Make Me a Hanzi, 22 June 2019)
source.variation: The cited PRC-order dataset supplies two ordered strokes for 力. Median 1 draws a horizontal that turns down and hooks to the left without lifting; median 2 a long left-falling stroke from above it, down through it to the lower left. These are the last two strokes of 男. Make Me a Hanzi documents that its stroke paths are ordered in proper stroke order, its medians use the same coordinate system for stroke-order animation, and the project follows People's Republic of China stroke order. This learner path adapts those two ordered medians to the vendored Noto Sans SC outline while preserving their order, their directions, the turn, the hook and one intervening pen lifts; stroke widths and proportions differ between the Arphic-derived source graphics and Noto Sans SC.

source.citation: Hanzi Writer Data 包.json, ordered stroke paths and medians 1–5 (Hanzi Writer Data snapshot 68d10a4, updated from Make Me a Hanzi, 22 June 2019)
source.variation: The cited PRC-order dataset supplies five ordered strokes for 包, in two pieces. Medians 1–2 draw 勹: a left-falling stroke, then a horizontal that turns down the right side and hooks to the left without lifting. Medians 3–5 draw 巳 inside: a horizontal that turns down without lifting, a horizontal, then a vertical that bends right along the foot and hooks up without lifting, as 也 ends. Make Me a Hanzi documents that its stroke paths are ordered in proper stroke order, its medians use the same coordinate system for stroke-order animation, and the project follows People's Republic of China stroke order. This learner path adapts those five ordered medians to the vendored Noto Sans SC outline while preserving their order, their directions, the turns, the two hooks and four intervening pen lifts; stroke widths and proportions differ between the Arphic-derived source graphics and Noto Sans SC.

source.citation: Hanzi Writer Data 北.json, ordered stroke paths and medians 1–5 (Hanzi Writer Data snapshot 68d10a4, updated from Make Me a Hanzi, 22 June 2019)
source.variation: The cited PRC-order dataset supplies five ordered strokes for 北, in two halves. Medians 1–3 draw the left half: a vertical, a short horizontal from the left into it, then a stroke rising to the right into its foot. Medians 4–5 draw the right half as 比 ends: a left-falling stroke, then a vertical that bends right along the foot and hooks up without lifting. Make Me a Hanzi documents that its stroke paths are ordered in proper stroke order, its medians use the same coordinate system for stroke-order animation, and the project follows People's Republic of China stroke order. This learner path adapts those five ordered medians to the vendored Noto Sans SC outline while preserving their order, their directions, the hook and four intervening pen lifts; stroke widths and proportions differ between the Arphic-derived source graphics and Noto Sans SC.

source.citation: Hanzi Writer Data 区.json, ordered stroke paths and medians 1–4 (Hanzi Writer Data snapshot 68d10a4, updated from Make Me a Hanzi, 22 June 2019)
source.variation: The cited PRC-order dataset supplies four ordered strokes for 区. Median 1 draws the top horizontal; medians 2–3 the cross inside, a left-falling stroke and then a stroke falling to the right across it; median 4 a vertical down the left side that turns right along the foot without lifting, closing the frame last. Make Me a Hanzi documents that its stroke paths are ordered in proper stroke order, its medians use the same coordinate system for stroke-order animation, and the project follows People's Republic of China stroke order. This learner path adapts those four ordered medians to the vendored Noto Sans SC outline while preserving their order, their directions, the turn and three intervening pen lifts; stroke widths and proportions differ between the Arphic-derived source graphics and Noto Sans SC.

source.citation: Hanzi Writer Data 医.json, ordered stroke paths and medians 1–7 (Hanzi Writer Data snapshot 68d10a4, updated from Make Me a Hanzi, 22 June 2019)
source.variation: The cited PRC-order dataset supplies seven ordered strokes for 医, in two pieces, the frame opened first and closed last. Median 1 draws the frame's top horizontal. Medians 2–6 draw inside it a short left-falling stroke and a short horizontal, then a long horizontal, a long left-falling stroke through it and a dot, as 头 ends. Median 7 closes the frame: a vertical down the left side that turns right along the foot without lifting. Make Me a Hanzi documents that its stroke paths are ordered in proper stroke order, its medians use the same coordinate system for stroke-order animation, and the project follows People's Republic of China stroke order. This learner path adapts those seven ordered medians to the vendored Noto Sans SC outline while preserving their order, their directions, the turn and six intervening pen lifts; stroke widths and proportions differ between the Arphic-derived source graphics and Noto Sans SC.

source.variation: The cited PRC-order dataset supplies two ordered strokes for 十: median 1 crosses from left to right, median 2 descends through its centre. Horizontal before vertical, the same order 三 and 四 already used. The character is the lower component of 早 and appeared in this course as a part of that character for thirteen chapters before it was taught on its own.

source.citation: Hanzi Writer Data 千.json, ordered stroke paths and medians 1–3 (Hanzi Writer Data snapshot 68d10a4, updated from Make Me a Hanzi, 22 June 2019)
source.variation: The cited PRC-order dataset supplies three ordered strokes for 千. Median 1 draws a short left-falling stroke across the top; medians 2–3 draw 十 under it as 十 is written alone: the horizontal, then the vertical through it. Make Me a Hanzi documents that its stroke paths are ordered in proper stroke order, its medians use the same coordinate system for stroke-order animation, and the project follows People's Republic of China stroke order. This learner path adapts those three ordered medians to the vendored Noto Sans SC outline while preserving their order, their directions and two intervening pen lifts; stroke widths and proportions differ between the Arphic-derived source graphics and Noto Sans SC.

source.variation: The cited PRC-order dataset supplies eight ordered strokes for 卖, in two pieces. Medians 1–2 draw a small 十: a short horizontal, then a short vertical through it. Medians 3–8 draw 买 as 买 is written alone: a horizontal that hooks down to the left without lifting, two dots, a long horizontal, a left-falling stroke through it, then the last stroke at the lower right. Make Me a Hanzi documents that its stroke paths are ordered in proper stroke order, its medians use the same coordinate system for stroke-order animation, and the project follows People's Republic of China stroke order. This learner path adapts those eight ordered medians to the vendored Noto Sans SC outline while preserving their order, their directions, the turn and seven intervening pen lifts; stroke widths and proportions differ between the Arphic-derived source graphics and Noto Sans SC.

source.citation: Hanzi Writer Data 南.json, ordered stroke paths and medians 1–9 (Hanzi Writer Data snapshot 68d10a4, updated from Make Me a Hanzi, 22 June 2019)
source.variation: The cited PRC-order dataset supplies nine ordered strokes for 南, in three pieces. Medians 1–2 draw 十 on top as 十 is written alone: the horizontal, then the vertical through it. Medians 3–4 draw the frame as 高 draws it: its left side, then a horizontal that turns down the right side and hooks to the left without lifting. Medians 5–9 draw the inside: a dot and a short left-falling stroke, two horizontals, then a vertical from the upper horizontal down through the lower one. Make Me a Hanzi documents that its stroke paths are ordered in proper stroke order, its medians use the same coordinate system for stroke-order animation, and the project follows People's Republic of China stroke order. This learner path adapts those nine ordered medians to the vendored Noto Sans SC outline while preserving their order, their directions, the turn, the hook and eight intervening pen lifts; stroke widths and proportions differ between the Arphic-derived source graphics and Noto Sans SC.

source.citation: Hanzi Writer Data 原.json, ordered stroke paths and medians 1–10 (Hanzi Writer Data snapshot 68d10a4, updated from Make Me a Hanzi, 22 June 2019)
source.variation: The cited PRC-order dataset supplies ten ordered strokes for 原, in three pieces. Medians 1–10 draw the first ten strokes of 愿: the cliff (a horizontal and a long left-falling stroke from its left end), then 白, then 小. Make Me a Hanzi documents that its stroke paths are ordered in proper stroke order, its medians use the same coordinate system for stroke-order animation, and the project follows People's Republic of China stroke order. This learner path adapts those ten ordered medians to the vendored Noto Sans SC outline while preserving their order, their directions, the turn, the hook and nine intervening pen lifts; stroke widths and proportions differ between the Arphic-derived source graphics and Noto Sans SC.

source.citation: Hanzi Writer Data 去.json, ordered stroke paths and medians 1–5 (Hanzi Writer Data snapshot 68d10a4, updated from Make Me a Hanzi, 22 June 2019)
source.variation: The cited PRC-order dataset supplies five ordered strokes for 去, in two pieces. Medians 1–3 draw 土 on top: the upper horizontal, the vertical through it, then the long horizontal it stands on. Medians 4–5 draw 厶 under it: a stroke that falls to the lower left and turns right along the foot without lifting, then a dot. Make Me a Hanzi documents that its stroke paths are ordered in proper stroke order, its medians use the same coordinate system for stroke-order animation, and the project follows People's Republic of China stroke order. This learner path adapts those five ordered medians to the vendored Noto Sans SC outline while preserving their order, their directions, the turn and four intervening pen lifts; stroke widths and proportions differ between the Arphic-derived source graphics and Noto Sans SC.

source.citation: Hanzi Writer Data 口.json, ordered stroke paths and medians 1–3 (Hanzi Writer Data snapshot 68d10a4, updated from Make Me a Hanzi, 22 June 2019)
source.variation: The cited PRC-order dataset supplies three ordered strokes for 口. Median 1 starts at the upper left and descends the left side; median 2 restarts near the upper left, crosses the top from left to right, turns without lifting, then descends the right side; median 3 restarts at the lower left and closes the bottom from left to right. Make Me a Hanzi documents that its stroke paths are ordered in proper stroke order, its medians use the same coordinate system for stroke-order animation, and the project follows People's Republic of China stroke order. This learner path adapts those three ordered medians to the vendored Noto Sans SC outline while preserving their directions, the joined corner, and two intervening pen lifts; stroke widths and proportions differ between the Arphic-derived source graphics and Noto Sans SC.

source.variation: The cited PRC-order dataset supplies five ordered strokes for 古, in two pieces. Medians 1–2 draw 十: a long horizontal, then a vertical down through its middle. Medians 3–5 draw 口 under it in the order the standalone character uses. These are the first five strokes of 故. Make Me a Hanzi documents that its stroke paths are ordered in proper stroke order, its medians use the same coordinate system for stroke-order animation, and the project follows People's Republic of China stroke order. This learner path adapts those five ordered medians to the vendored Noto Sans SC outline while preserving their order, their directions, the turn and four intervening pen lifts; stroke widths and proportions differ between the Arphic-derived source graphics and Noto Sans SC.

source.citation: Hanzi Writer Data 只.json, ordered stroke paths and medians 1–5 (Hanzi Writer Data snapshot 68d10a4, updated from Make Me a Hanzi, 22 June 2019)
source.variation: The cited PRC-order dataset supplies five ordered strokes for 只, in two pieces. Medians 1–3 draw 口 on top in the order the standalone character uses. Medians 4–5 draw 八 under it: a left-falling stroke, then a dot. Make Me a Hanzi documents that its stroke paths are ordered in proper stroke order, its medians use the same coordinate system for stroke-order animation, and the project follows People's Republic of China stroke order. This learner path adapts those five ordered medians to the vendored Noto Sans SC outline while preserving their order, their directions, the turn and four intervening pen lifts; stroke widths and proportions differ between the Arphic-derived source graphics and Noto Sans SC.

source.citation: Hanzi Writer Data 叫.json, ordered stroke paths and medians 1–5 (Hanzi Writer Data snapshot 68d10a4, updated from Make Me a Hanzi, 22 June 2019)
source.variation: The cited PRC-order dataset supplies five ordered strokes for 叫, in two pieces. Medians 1–3 draw 口 on the left in the order the standalone character uses: its left side, its joined top and right side, and its closing bottom. Medians 4–5 draw the right side: a vertical that flicks up to the right at its foot without lifting, then a long vertical from the top to the baseline. Make Me a Hanzi documents that its stroke paths are ordered in proper stroke order, its medians use the same coordinate system for stroke-order animation, and the project follows People's Republic of China stroke order. This learner path adapts those five ordered medians to the vendored Noto Sans SC outline while preserving their order, their directions, the turn, the flick and four intervening pen lifts; stroke widths and proportions differ between the Arphic-derived source graphics and Noto Sans SC.

source.citation: Hanzi Writer Data 可.json, ordered stroke paths and medians 1–5 (Hanzi Writer Data snapshot 68d10a4, updated from Make Me a Hanzi, 22 June 2019)
source.variation: The cited PRC-order dataset supplies five ordered strokes for 可. Median 1 draws a long horizontal across the top; medians 2–4 a small 口 under it in the order the standalone character uses; median 5 a long vertical down the right side from the horizontal, hooking to the left at its foot without lifting. Make Me a Hanzi documents that its stroke paths are ordered in proper stroke order, its medians use the same coordinate system for stroke-order animation, and the project follows People's Republic of China stroke order. This learner path adapts those five ordered medians to the vendored Noto Sans SC outline while preserving their order, their directions, the turn, the hook and four intervening pen lifts; stroke widths and proportions differ between the Arphic-derived source graphics and Noto Sans SC.

source.citation: Hanzi Writer Data 吃.json, ordered stroke paths and medians 1–6 (Hanzi Writer Data snapshot 68d10a4, updated from Make Me a Hanzi, 22 June 2019)
source.variation: The cited PRC-order dataset supplies six ordered strokes for 吃, in two pieces. Medians 1–3 draw 口 on the left in the order the standalone character uses. Medians 4–6 draw 乞 on the right: a short left-falling stroke, a horizontal, then a horizontal that turns down to the left, runs along the foot and hooks up without lifting. Make Me a Hanzi documents that its stroke paths are ordered in proper stroke order, its medians use the same coordinate system for stroke-order animation, and the project follows People's Republic of China stroke order. This learner path adapts those six ordered medians to the vendored Noto Sans SC outline while preserving their order, their directions, the turns, the hook and five intervening pen lifts; stroke widths and proportions differ between the Arphic-derived source graphics and Noto Sans SC. Noto's last stroke turns further right than the source's.

source.variation: The cited PRC-order dataset supplies six ordered strokes for 名. Medians 1–3 draw 夕 first: an upper left-falling stroke, a separately started horizontal that continues down-left without lifting, and a separately placed inner down-right dot. Medians 4–6 then draw 口: the left vertical, a separately started top horizontal that turns down the right side without lifting, and the closing bottom horizontal. Make Me a Hanzi documents proper People's Republic of China stroke order and matching animation medians. This learner path adapts all six medians to Noto Sans SC while preserving their order, both joined turns, and five intervening lifts; Noto's 夕 sweep is broader and 口 is squarer than the Arphic-derived source graphic.

source.variation: The cited PRC-order dataset supplies six ordered strokes for 后, in two pieces. Medians 1–3 draw the frame: a short left-falling stroke across the top, a long left-falling stroke down the left side, then the horizontal. Medians 4–6 draw 口 inside it in the order the standalone character uses. Make Me a Hanzi documents that its stroke paths are ordered in proper stroke order, its medians use the same coordinate system for stroke-order animation, and the project follows People's Republic of China stroke order. This learner path adapts those six ordered medians to the vendored Noto Sans SC outline while preserving their order, their directions, the turn and five intervening pen lifts; stroke widths and proportions differ between the Arphic-derived source graphics and Noto Sans SC.

source.citation: Hanzi Writer Data 吗.json, ordered stroke paths and medians 1–6 (Hanzi Writer Data snapshot 68d10a4, updated from Make Me a Hanzi, 22 June 2019)
source.variation: The cited PRC-order dataset supplies six ordered strokes for 吗. Medians 1–3 draw the left 口 in the same order the standalone character uses: its left vertical, its joined top and right sides, and its closing bottom horizontal, all inside the upper-left third of the square. Medians 4–6 then draw 马: a horizontal that turns down at the right, a long stroke that turns twice and hooks, and a wide finishing horizontal that runs almost the full width of the character and is the widest stroke in it. Make Me a Hanzi documents that its stroke paths are ordered in proper stroke order, its medians use the same coordinate system for stroke-order animation, and the project follows People's Republic of China stroke order. This learner path adapts those six ordered medians to the vendored Noto Sans SC outline while preserving their order, directions, the two joined corners and five intervening pen lifts; stroke widths and proportions differ between the Arphic-derived source graphics and Noto Sans SC.

source.citation: Hanzi Writer Data 吵.json, ordered stroke paths and medians 1–7 (Hanzi Writer Data snapshot 68d10a4, updated from Make Me a Hanzi, 22 June 2019)
source.variation: The cited PRC-order dataset supplies seven ordered strokes for 吵, in two pieces. Medians 1–3 draw 口 on the left in the order the standalone character uses. Medians 4–7 draw 少 on the right as 少 is written alone: the vertical, a short stroke on the left, a dot on the right, then the long left-falling stroke. Make Me a Hanzi documents that its stroke paths are ordered in proper stroke order, its medians use the same coordinate system for stroke-order animation, and the project follows People's Republic of China stroke order. This learner path adapts those seven ordered medians to the vendored Noto Sans SC outline while preserving their order, their directions, the turn and six intervening pen lifts; stroke widths and proportions differ between the Arphic-derived source graphics and Noto Sans SC.

source.variation: The cited PRC-order dataset supplies eight ordered strokes for 呢. Medians 1–3 draw the left 口 in the same order the standalone character uses and in the same upper-left third of the square that 吗 puts it in. Medians 4–6 draw 尸 — a turning top stroke, a horizontal, and a long left-falling stroke that runs past the bottom of 口 — and medians 7–8 draw 匕 tucked inside it. Make Me a Hanzi documents proper People's Republic of China stroke order and matching animation medians. This learner path adapts all eight medians to Noto Sans SC while preserving their order, the three internal turns and seven intervening lifts; Noto sets 尸's long falling stroke slightly steeper than the Arphic-derived source graphic.

source.citation: Hanzi Writer Data 味.json, ordered stroke paths and medians 1–8 (Hanzi Writer Data snapshot 68d10a4, updated from Make Me a Hanzi, 22 June 2019)
source.variation: The cited PRC-order dataset supplies eight ordered strokes for 味, in two pieces. Medians 1–3 draw 口 in the order the standalone character uses. Medians 4–8 draw the right side: a short horizontal, a longer horizontal under it, a vertical down through both, then a left-falling stroke and a right-falling stroke from the crossing. Make Me a Hanzi documents that its stroke paths are ordered in proper stroke order, its medians use the same coordinate system for stroke-order animation, and the project follows People's Republic of China stroke order. This learner path adapts those eight ordered medians to the vendored Noto Sans SC outline while preserving their order, their directions, the turn and seven intervening pen lifts; stroke widths and proportions differ between the Arphic-derived source graphics and Noto Sans SC.

source.variation: The cited PRC-order dataset supplies eight ordered strokes for 和. Medians 1–5 draw 禾: the short top left-falling stroke, the horizontal, the long central vertical, then the left-falling and right-falling pair that finish it. Medians 6–8 draw 口 on the right in the same order the standalone character uses. Left component complete before the right one begins. Make Me a Hanzi documents proper People's Republic of China stroke order and matching animation medians. This learner path adapts all eight medians to Noto Sans SC while preserving their order, the joined corner in 口 and seven intervening lifts; Noto compresses 禾's final right-falling stroke into a dot, as the source graphic does, because 口 stands beside it.

source.citation: Hanzi Writer Data 哪.json, ordered stroke paths and medians 1–9 (Hanzi Writer Data snapshot 68d10a4, updated from Make Me a Hanzi, 22 June 2019)
source.variation: The cited PRC-order dataset supplies nine ordered strokes for 哪, in two pieces. Medians 1–3 draw 口 on the left in the order the standalone character uses. Medians 4–9 draw 那 on the right in the order 那 is written alone: a horizontal that turns down the right side and hooks to the left without lifting, two horizontals, a left-falling stroke through them, then 阝: a stroke that runs right, falls back, swells round to the right and hooks to the left without lifting, and the vertical. Make Me a Hanzi documents that its stroke paths are ordered in proper stroke order, its medians use the same coordinate system for stroke-order animation, and the project follows People's Republic of China stroke order. This learner path adapts those nine ordered medians to the vendored Noto Sans SC outline while preserving their order, their directions, the turns, the two hooks and eight intervening pen lifts; stroke widths and proportions differ between the Arphic-derived source graphics and Noto Sans SC.

source.citation: Hanzi Writer Data 喜.json, ordered stroke paths and medians 1–12 (Hanzi Writer Data snapshot 68d10a4, updated from Make Me a Hanzi, 22 June 2019)
source.variation: The cited PRC-order dataset supplies twelve ordered strokes for 喜, and they descend the character in four bands: medians 1–3 the 士 at the top, medians 4–6 a 口, medians 7–8 the short pair beneath it, median 9 the single widest horizontal in the character, and medians 10–12 the closing 口. Top before bottom throughout, and each 口 is built left side, joined top-and-right, closing floor — the order the reader already writes. Make Me a Hanzi documents proper People's Republic of China stroke order and matching animation medians. This learner path adapts all twelve medians to Noto Sans SC while preserving their order, the two joined corners and eleven intervening lifts; Noto's ninth stroke runs slightly wider than the Arphic-derived source graphic's.

source.citation: Hanzi Writer Data 喝.json, ordered stroke paths and medians 1–12 (Hanzi Writer Data snapshot 68d10a4, updated from Make Me a Hanzi, 22 June 2019)
source.variation: The cited PRC-order dataset supplies twelve ordered strokes for 喝, in two pieces. Medians 1–3 draw 口 on the left. Medians 4–12 draw 曷 on the right: 日 first, as 日 is written alone (its left side, the joined top and right side, the middle horizontal, the closing bottom), then a short left-falling stroke, a horizontal that turns down the right side and hooks to the left without lifting, a left-falling stroke and a dot inside it, and last a vertical that turns along the foot without lifting. Make Me a Hanzi documents that its stroke paths are ordered in proper stroke order, its medians use the same coordinate system for stroke-order animation, and the project follows People's Republic of China stroke order. This learner path adapts those twelve ordered medians to the vendored Noto Sans SC outline while preserving their order, their directions, the turns, the hook and eleven intervening pen lifts; stroke widths and proportions differ between the Arphic-derived source graphics and Noto Sans SC.

source.citation: Hanzi Writer Data 四.json, ordered stroke paths and medians 1–5 (Hanzi Writer Data snapshot 68d10a4, updated from Make Me a Hanzi, 22 June 2019)
source.variation: The cited PRC-order dataset supplies five ordered strokes for 四. Medians 1–2 build the outer box exactly as 口 does — the left side, then the top and right in one turning stroke; medians 3–4 are the two pieces inside it; median 5 closes the bottom last. Make Me a Hanzi documents that its stroke paths are ordered in proper stroke order, its medians use the same coordinate system for stroke-order animation, and the project follows People's Republic of China stroke order. This learner path adapts those ordered medians to the vendored Noto Sans SC outline while preserving their directions and pen lifts; stroke widths and proportions differ between the Arphic-derived source graphics and Noto Sans SC.

source.citation: Hanzi Writer Data 回.json, ordered stroke paths and medians 1–6 (Hanzi Writer Data snapshot 68d10a4, updated from Make Me a Hanzi, 22 June 2019)
source.variation: The cited PRC-order dataset supplies six ordered strokes for 回, in two pieces. Medians 1–2 draw the large frame's left side, then a horizontal that turns down its right side without lifting. Medians 3–5 draw a small 口 inside it in the order the standalone character uses. Median 6 closes the large frame along the foot, as 国 closes. Make Me a Hanzi documents that its stroke paths are ordered in proper stroke order, its medians use the same coordinate system for stroke-order animation, and the project follows People's Republic of China stroke order. This learner path adapts those six ordered medians to the vendored Noto Sans SC outline while preserving their order, their directions, the turns and five intervening pen lifts; stroke widths and proportions differ between the Arphic-derived source graphics and Noto Sans SC.

source.citation: Hanzi Writer Data 因.json, ordered stroke paths and medians 1–6 (Hanzi Writer Data snapshot 68d10a4, updated from Make Me a Hanzi, 22 June 2019)
source.variation: The cited PRC-order dataset supplies six ordered strokes for 因. Medians 1–2 open the enclosure as 国 does: its left side, then a horizontal that turns down the right side without lifting; medians 3–5 draw 大 inside as 大 is written alone; median 6 closes the enclosure along the foot. Make Me a Hanzi documents that its stroke paths are ordered in proper stroke order, its medians use the same coordinate system for stroke-order animation, and the project follows People's Republic of China stroke order. This learner path adapts those six ordered medians to the vendored Noto Sans SC outline while preserving their order, their directions, the turn and five intervening pen lifts; stroke widths and proportions differ between the Arphic-derived source graphics and Noto Sans SC.

source.citation: Hanzi Writer Data 图.json, ordered stroke paths and medians 1–8 (Hanzi Writer Data snapshot 68d10a4, updated from Make Me a Hanzi, 22 June 2019)
source.variation: The cited PRC-order dataset supplies eight ordered strokes for 图. Medians 1–2 open the frame as 国 does: its left side, then a horizontal that turns down the right side without lifting. Medians 3–7 draw the inside: a short left-falling stroke, a horizontal that turns and falls to the left without lifting, a right-falling stroke across it, then two dots, one under the other. Median 8 closes the frame along the foot. Make Me a Hanzi documents that its stroke paths are ordered in proper stroke order, its medians use the same coordinate system for stroke-order animation, and the project follows People's Republic of China stroke order. This learner path adapts those eight ordered medians to the vendored Noto Sans SC outline while preserving their order, their directions, the turns and seven intervening pen lifts; stroke widths and proportions differ between the Arphic-derived source graphics and Noto Sans SC.

This learner path adapts those six ordered medians to the vendored Noto Sans SC outline while preserving their order, their directions, the turns, the hooks and five intervening pen lifts; stroke widths and proportions differ between the Arphic-derived source graphics and Noto Sans SC.

source.citation: Hanzi Writer Data 城.json, ordered stroke paths and medians 1–9 (Hanzi Writer Data snapshot 68d10a4, updated from Make Me a Hanzi, 22 June 2019)
source.variation: The cited PRC-order dataset supplies nine ordered strokes for 城, in two pieces. Medians 1–3 draw the earth piece as 地 opens: a short horizontal, a vertical through it, then a stroke rising to the right. Medians 4–9 draw 成 as 成 is written alone: a horizontal, a long left-falling stroke from its left end, a short horizontal that turns down and hooks to the left without lifting, a long slanting stroke that hooks up at its foot without lifting, a short left-falling stroke across it, then a dot at the top right. Make Me a Hanzi documents that its stroke paths are ordered in proper stroke order, its medians use the same coordinate system for stroke-order animation, and the project follows People's Republic of China stroke order. This learner path adapts those nine ordered medians to the vendored Noto Sans SC outline while preserving their order, their directions, the turns, the hooks and eight intervening pen lifts; stroke widths and proportions differ between the Arphic-derived source graphics and Noto Sans SC.

source.citation: Hanzi Writer Data 多.json, ordered stroke paths and medians 1–6 (Hanzi Writer Data snapshot 68d10a4, updated from Make Me a Hanzi, 22 June 2019)
source.variation: The cited PRC-order dataset supplies six ordered strokes for 多, in two pieces, the same three strokes twice. Medians 1–3 draw the upper 夕: a short left-falling stroke, a horizontal that turns to fall to the lower left without lifting, then a dot inside. Medians 4–6 draw the lower 夕 in the same order, larger. Make Me a Hanzi documents that its stroke paths are ordered in proper stroke order, its medians use the same coordinate system for stroke-order animation, and the project follows People's Republic of China stroke order. This learner path adapts those six ordered medians to the vendored Noto Sans SC outline while preserving their order, their directions, the two turns and five intervening pen lifts; stroke widths and proportions differ between the Arphic-derived source graphics and Noto Sans SC.

source.citation: Hanzi Writer Data 女.json, ordered stroke paths and medians 1–3 (Hanzi Writer Data snapshot 68d10a4, updated from Make Me a Hanzi, 22 June 2019)
source.variation: The cited PRC-order dataset supplies three ordered strokes for 女. Median 1 starts near the upper centre, makes a short down-right entry, bends down-left to the lower-left junction, then turns without lifting and sweeps down-right to finish; median 2 restarts at the upper right and falls down-left; median 3 restarts at the left edge and crosses the middle from left to right. Make Me a Hanzi documents that its stroke paths are ordered in proper stroke order, its medians use the same coordinate system for stroke-order animation, and the project follows People's Republic of China stroke order. This learner path adapts those three ordered medians to the vendored Noto Sans SC outline while preserving their directions, the first stroke's internal turn, and two intervening pen lifts; stroke widths and proportions differ between the Arphic-derived source graphics and Noto Sans SC.

source.citation: Hanzi Writer Data 好.json, ordered stroke paths and medians 1–6 (Hanzi Writer Data snapshot 68d10a4, updated from Make Me a Hanzi, 22 June 2019)
source.variation: The cited PRC-order dataset supplies six ordered strokes for 好. Medians 1–3 draw 女 first: a bent stroke descends down-left and sweeps right without lifting, a separately started stroke falls down-left, and a separately started horizontal crosses left-to-right. Medians 4–6 then draw 子: a horizontal turns down-left without lifting, a separately started vertical descends and hooks left without lifting, and a separately started middle horizontal crosses left-to-right. Make Me a Hanzi documents that its stroke paths are ordered in proper stroke order, its medians use the same coordinate system for stroke-order animation, and the project follows People's Republic of China stroke order. This learner path adapts those six ordered medians to the vendored Noto Sans SC outline while preserving their directions, 女-before-子 component order, all three joined turns, and five intervening pen lifts; Noto's 子 top turn is more angular and its vertical hook is flatter than the source medians, and stroke widths and proportions differ between the Arphic-derived source graphics and Noto Sans SC.

This learner path adapts those six ordered medians to the vendored Noto Sans SC outline while preserving their order, their directions, the four turns, the hook and five intervening pen lifts; stroke widths and proportions differ between the Arphic-derived source graphics and Noto Sans SC. Noto's narrow 女 crosses its horizontal higher than the source's.

source.variation: The cited PRC-order dataset supplies three ordered strokes for 子. Median 1 starts at the upper left, crosses the top from left to right, then turns without lifting and sweeps down-left; median 2 restarts below the upper-left turn, descends through the centre, then hooks left at the base without lifting; median 3 restarts at the left edge and crosses the middle from left to right. Make Me a Hanzi documents that its stroke paths are ordered in proper stroke order, its medians use the same coordinate system for stroke-order animation, and the project follows People's Republic of China stroke order. This learner path adapts those three ordered medians to the vendored Noto Sans SC outline while preserving their directions, both internal turns, and two intervening pen lifts; the Noto base hook is flatter than the source median, and stroke widths and proportions differ between the Arphic-derived source graphics and Noto Sans SC.

source.variation: The cited PRC-order dataset supplies six ordered strokes for 字. Medians 1–3 draw 宀 first: a down-right top dot, a separately started left-side down-left stroke, and a separately started horizontal roof that hooks down-left without lifting. Medians 4–6 then draw 子: a top horizontal that turns down-left without lifting, a separately started vertical that hooks left without lifting, and a final middle horizontal. Make Me a Hanzi documents proper People's Republic of China stroke order and matching animation medians. This learner path adapts all six medians to Noto Sans SC while preserving their order, all three joined turns, and five intervening lifts; Noto's roof is wider and 子's vertical hook is flatter than the Arphic-derived source graphic.

source.citation: Hanzi Writer Data 季.json, ordered stroke paths and medians 1–8 (Hanzi Writer Data snapshot 68d10a4, updated from Make Me a Hanzi, 22 June 2019)
source.variation: The cited PRC-order dataset supplies eight ordered strokes for 季, in two pieces. Medians 1–5 draw the grain piece on top as 秋 opens, spread wide: a short flat left-falling stroke, a horizontal, a vertical down through it, a left-falling stroke from the crossing, then a long right-falling stroke. Medians 6–8 draw 子 as 子 is written alone: a horizontal that turns and falls to the left without lifting, a vertical that hooks to the left, then a horizontal across. Make Me a Hanzi documents that its stroke paths are ordered in proper stroke order, its medians use the same coordinate system for stroke-order animation, and the project follows People's Republic of China stroke order. This learner path adapts those eight ordered medians to the vendored Noto Sans SC outline while preserving their order, their directions, the turn, the hook and seven intervening pen lifts; stroke widths and proportions differ between the Arphic-derived source graphics and Noto Sans SC.

source.citation: Hanzi Writer Data 孩.json, ordered stroke paths and medians 1–9 (Hanzi Writer Data snapshot 68d10a4, updated from Make Me a Hanzi, 22 June 2019)
source.variation: The cited PRC-order dataset supplies nine ordered strokes for 孩, in two pieces. Medians 1–3 draw 子 on the left: a horizontal that turns down to the left without lifting, a vertical that hooks to the left at its foot without lifting, then a stroke rising to the right. Medians 4–9 draw the right side: a dot, a horizontal, a stroke that falls to the left and turns up to the right without lifting, two left-falling strokes, then a dot at the lower right. Make Me a Hanzi documents that its stroke paths are ordered in proper stroke order, its medians use the same coordinate system for stroke-order animation, and the project follows People's Republic of China stroke order. This learner path adapts those nine ordered medians to the vendored Noto Sans SC outline while preserving their order, their directions, the turns, the hook and eight intervening pen lifts; stroke widths and proportions differ between the Arphic-derived source graphics and Noto Sans SC.

Medians 4–6 draw 女 under it as 妈 opens: a stroke that falls to the left and turns down to the right without lifting, a left-falling stroke, then a long horizontal. Make Me a Hanzi documents that its stroke paths are ordered in proper stroke order, its medians use the same coordinate system for stroke-order animation, and the project follows People's Republic of China stroke order. This learner path adapts those six ordered medians to the vendored Noto Sans SC outline while preserving their order, their directions, the turns and five intervening pen lifts; stroke widths and proportions differ between the Arphic-derived source graphics and Noto Sans SC. Noto's roof turns straight down at its right end, where the source's hooks to the left.

source.citation: Hanzi Writer Data 客.json, ordered stroke paths and medians 1–9 (Hanzi Writer Data snapshot 68d10a4, updated from Make Me a Hanzi, 22 June 2019)
source.variation: The cited PRC-order dataset supplies nine ordered strokes for 客, in two pieces. Medians 1–3 draw the roof piece 宀 as 家 opens: a dot, the left side, then a horizontal that hooks down at the right without lifting. Medians 4–9 draw 各 under it: a left-falling stroke, a horizontal that turns to fall to the lower left without lifting, the right-falling stroke across it, then 口 in the order the standalone character uses. Make Me a Hanzi documents that its stroke paths are ordered in proper stroke order, its medians use the same coordinate system for stroke-order animation, and the project follows People's Republic of China stroke order. This learner path adapts those nine ordered medians to the vendored Noto Sans SC outline while preserving their order, their directions, the turns, the hook and eight intervening pen lifts; stroke widths and proportions differ between the Arphic-derived source graphics and Noto Sans SC.

source.citation: Hanzi Writer Data 家.json, ordered stroke paths and medians 1–10 (Hanzi Writer Data snapshot 68d10a4, updated from Make Me a Hanzi, 22 June 2019)
source.variation: The cited PRC-order dataset supplies ten ordered strokes for 家. Medians 1–3 complete 宀 from the top dot through the hooked roof; medians 4–10 then complete the lower body from its top horizontal through the central curve, three left-falling strokes, and final right-falling stroke. Make Me a Hanzi documents that its stroke paths are ordered in proper stroke order, its medians use the same coordinate system for stroke-order animation, and the project follows People's Republic of China stroke order. This learner path adapts those ten ordered medians to the vendored Noto Sans SC outline while preserving their directions, the roof-before-body order, each unbroken turn, and nine intervening pen lifts; stroke widths and proportions differ between the Arphic-derived source graphics and Noto Sans SC.

source.citation: Hanzi Writer Data 尔.json, ordered stroke paths and medians 1–5 (Hanzi Writer Data snapshot 68d10a4, updated from Make Me a Hanzi, 22 June 2019)
source.variation: The cited PRC-order dataset supplies five ordered strokes for 尔, the same five that close 你. Median 1 starts at the top and falls down-left; median 2 restarts below it, crosses rightward, then hooks down-left without lifting; median 3 restarts at the centre, descends, then hooks left without lifting; medians 4-5 separately draw the lower-left dot down-left and the lower-right dot down-right. Make Me a Hanzi documents that its stroke paths are ordered in proper stroke order, its medians use the same coordinate system for stroke-order animation, and the project follows People's Republic of China stroke order. This learner path adapts those five ordered medians to the vendored Noto Sans SC outline while preserving their directions, the two unbroken hooks and the four intervening pen lifts; stroke widths and proportions differ between the Arphic-derived source graphics and Noto Sans SC.

frames.label: draw the upper left-falling stroke
lift, then draw the upper horizontal from left to right
hook down and left without lifting
lift, then descend the central vertical
hook left at the base without lifting
lift, then draw the lower-left dot down and left
lift, then draw the lower-right dot down and right

source.citation: Hanzi Writer Data 就.json, ordered stroke paths and medians 1–12 (Hanzi Writer Data snapshot 68d10a4, updated from Make Me a Hanzi, 22 June 2019)
source.variation: The cited PRC-order dataset supplies twelve ordered strokes for 就, in two pieces. Medians 1–8 draw the left side: a dot and a horizontal, 口 in the order the standalone character uses, then 小 (a vertical that hooks to the left at its foot without lifting, and two dots). Medians 9–12 draw the right side: a horizontal, a long left-falling stroke, a vertical that bends right along the foot and hooks up without lifting, then a dot. Make Me a Hanzi documents that its stroke paths are ordered in proper stroke order, its medians use the same coordinate system for stroke-order animation, and the project follows People's Republic of China stroke order. This learner path adapts those twelve ordered medians to the vendored Noto Sans SC outline while preserving their order, their directions, the turns, the hooks and eleven intervening pen lifts; stroke widths and proportions differ between the Arphic-derived source graphics and Noto Sans SC.

frames.label: draw the top dot
lift, then draw the horizontal
lift, then draw 口's left side
lift, then draw 口's top and turn down its right side
lift, then close 口 with a horizontal
lift, then draw 小's vertical and hook left
lift, then draw 小's left dot
lift, then draw 小's right dot

source.variation: The cited PRC-order dataset supplies six ordered strokes for 岁. Medians 1–3 draw 山 with its centre vertical first, then the joined left-and-base stroke, then the right vertical — centre before the sides, which is the one place this book's top-to-bottom and left-to-right rules do not decide the order by themselves. Medians 4–6 draw 夕 beneath. Make Me a Hanzi documents proper People's Republic of China stroke order and matching animation medians. This learner path adapts all six medians to Noto Sans SC while preserving their order, the two internal turns and five intervening lifts; Noto's 山 is wider and flatter than the Arphic-derived source graphic's.

source.variation: The cited PRC-order dataset supplies seven ordered strokes for 岛, in two pieces. Medians 1–4 draw the top: a short left-falling stroke, a small horizontal that turns down and hooks to the left without lifting, a dot inside it, then a stroke that runs down the left side, turns right along the foot, turns down again and hooks to the left without lifting. Medians 5–7 draw 山 as 山 is written alone: the middle vertical, the left side that turns right along the foot without lifting, then the right vertical. Make Me a Hanzi documents that its stroke paths are ordered in proper stroke order, its medians use the same coordinate system for stroke-order animation, and the project follows People's Republic of China stroke order. This learner path adapts those seven ordered medians to the vendored Noto Sans SC outline while preserving their order, their directions, the turns, the hooks and six intervening pen lifts; stroke widths and proportions differ between the Arphic-derived source graphics and Noto Sans SC.

source.citation: Hanzi Writer Data 常.json, ordered stroke paths and medians 1–11 (Hanzi Writer Data snapshot 68d10a4, updated from Make Me a Hanzi, 22 June 2019)
source.variation: The cited PRC-order dataset supplies eleven ordered strokes for 常, in four pieces. Medians 1–3 draw the three short strokes on top: a vertical in the middle, a dot to its left, then a short left-falling stroke to its right. Medians 4–5 draw the cover: a short stroke on the left, then a horizontal that hooks down to the left without lifting. Medians 6–8 draw 口 in the order the standalone character uses. Medians 9–11 draw 巾 at the foot: a short left vertical, a horizontal that turns down the right side and hooks to the left without lifting, then a long vertical down through the middle. Make Me a Hanzi documents that its stroke paths are ordered in proper stroke order, its medians use the same coordinate system for stroke-order animation, and the project follows People's Republic of China stroke order. This learner path adapts those eleven ordered medians to the vendored Noto Sans SC outline while preserving their order, their directions, the turns, the hooks and ten intervening pen lifts; stroke widths and proportions differ between the Arphic-derived source graphics and Noto Sans SC. Noto's cover turns straight down at its right end, where the source's hooks to the left.

source.citation: Hanzi Writer Data 年.json, ordered stroke paths and medians 1–6 (Hanzi Writer Data snapshot 68d10a4, updated from Make Me a Hanzi, 22 June 2019)
source.variation: The cited PRC-order dataset supplies six ordered strokes for 年. Median 1 draws a short left-falling stroke; medians 2–3 draw the upper and middle horizontals; median 4 draws the short vertical on the left down from the middle horizontal; median 5 draws the long horizontal; median 6 draws the long vertical last, from above the top horizontal through all three. Make Me a Hanzi documents that its stroke paths are ordered in proper stroke order, its medians use the same coordinate system for stroke-order animation, and the project follows People's Republic of China stroke order. This learner path adapts those six ordered medians to the vendored Noto Sans SC outline while preserving their order, their directions and five intervening pen lifts; stroke widths and proportions differ between the Arphic-derived source graphics and Noto Sans SC.

source.variation: The cited PRC-order dataset supplies seven ordered strokes for 应, in two pieces. Medians 1–3 draw the roof as 店 opens: a dot, a horizontal, then a long left-falling stroke down the left side. Medians 4–7 draw under it two dots, a left-falling stroke on the right, then a long horizontal along the foot. Make Me a Hanzi documents that its stroke paths are ordered in proper stroke order, its medians use the same coordinate system for stroke-order animation, and the project follows People's Republic of China stroke order. This learner path adapts those seven ordered medians to the vendored Noto Sans SC outline while preserving their order, their directions and six intervening pen lifts; stroke widths and proportions differ between the Arphic-derived source graphics and Noto Sans SC.

source.citation: Hanzi Writer Data 开.json, ordered stroke paths and medians 1–4 (Hanzi Writer Data snapshot 68d10a4, updated from Make Me a Hanzi, 22 June 2019)
source.variation: The cited PRC-order dataset supplies four ordered strokes for 开. Medians 1–2 draw the two horizontals, the lower one longer; median 3 draws the left leg, down through both and curving out to the lower left; median 4 draws the right leg, a vertical through both. Make Me a Hanzi documents that its stroke paths are ordered in proper stroke order, its medians use the same coordinate system for stroke-order animation, and the project follows People's Republic of China stroke order. This learner path adapts those four ordered medians to the vendored Noto Sans SC outline while preserving their order, their directions and three intervening pen lifts; stroke widths and proportions differ between the Arphic-derived source graphics and Noto Sans SC.
