source.citation: Hanzi Writer Data 当.json, ordered stroke paths and medians 1–6 (Hanzi Writer Data snapshot 68d10a4, updated from Make Me a Hanzi, 22 June 2019)
source.variation: The cited PRC-order dataset supplies six ordered strokes for 当, in two pieces. Medians 1–3 draw the three short strokes on top as 常 opens: a vertical in the middle, a dot to its left, then a short left-falling stroke to its right. Medians 4–6 draw the lower piece as 雪 ends: a horizontal that turns down its right side without lifting, then a horizontal across the middle and one along the foot. Make Me a Hanzi documents that its stroke paths are ordered in proper stroke order, its medians use the same coordinate system for stroke-order animation, and the project follows People's Republic of China stroke order. This learner path adapts those six ordered medians to the vendored Noto Sans SC outline while preserving their order, their directions, the turn and five intervening pen lifts; stroke widths and proportions differ between the Arphic-derived source graphics and Noto Sans SC.

source.citation: Hanzi Writer Data 往.json, ordered stroke paths and medians 1–8 (Hanzi Writer Data snapshot 68d10a4, updated from Make Me a Hanzi, 22 June 2019)
source.variation: The cited PRC-order dataset supplies eight ordered strokes for 往, in two pieces. Medians 1–3 draw 彳 on the left as 很 opens: two left-falling strokes, the upper one short, then a vertical. Medians 4–8 draw the right side: a dot, then 王 as 王 is written alone: two horizontals, a vertical down through them, then a long horizontal along the foot. Make Me a Hanzi documents that its stroke paths are ordered in proper stroke order, its medians use the same coordinate system for stroke-order animation, and the project follows People's Republic of China stroke order. This learner path adapts those eight ordered medians to the vendored Noto Sans SC outline while preserving their order, their directions and seven intervening pen lifts; stroke widths and proportions differ between the Arphic-derived source graphics and Noto Sans SC.

source.variation: The cited PRC-order dataset supplies four ordered strokes for 心. Median 1 draws the left dot; median 2 draws a curve that runs along the foot and hooks up without lifting; medians 3–4 draw the middle and right dots. These are the last four strokes of 想, in the same order. Make Me a Hanzi documents that its stroke paths are ordered in proper stroke order, its medians use the same coordinate system for stroke-order animation, and the project follows People's Republic of China stroke order. This learner path adapts those four ordered medians to the vendored Noto Sans SC outline while preserving their order, their directions, the turn, the hook and three intervening pen lifts; stroke widths and proportions differ between the Arphic-derived source graphics and Noto Sans SC.

source.citation: Hanzi Writer Data 怎.json, ordered stroke paths and medians 1–9 (Hanzi Writer Data snapshot 68d10a4, updated from Make Me a Hanzi, 22 June 2019)
source.variation: The cited PRC-order dataset supplies nine ordered strokes for 怎, in two pieces. Medians 1–5 draw the top as 作 ends: a short left-falling stroke, a horizontal to the right from it, a long vertical down from the horizontal, then two short horizontals to its right. Medians 6–9 draw 心 at the foot as 心 is written alone. Make Me a Hanzi documents that its stroke paths are ordered in proper stroke order, its medians use the same coordinate system for stroke-order animation, and the project follows People's Republic of China stroke order. This learner path adapts those nine ordered medians to the vendored Noto Sans SC outline while preserving their order, their directions, the hook and eight intervening pen lifts; stroke widths and proportions differ between the Arphic-derived source graphics and Noto Sans SC.

source.variation: The cited PRC-order dataset supplies eight ordered strokes for 怕, in two pieces. Medians 1–3 draw the upright heart as 快 opens. Medians 4–8 draw 白 as 白 is written alone: a short left-falling stroke at the top, its left side, a horizontal that turns down the right side without lifting, the middle horizontal, then the bottom that closes it. Make Me a Hanzi documents that its stroke paths are ordered in proper stroke order, its medians use the same coordinate system for stroke-order animation, and the project follows People's Republic of China stroke order. This learner path adapts those eight ordered medians to the vendored Noto Sans SC outline while preserving their order, their directions, the turn and seven intervening pen lifts; stroke widths and proportions differ between the Arphic-derived source graphics and Noto Sans SC.

source.citation: Hanzi Writer Data 性.json, ordered stroke paths and medians 1–8 (Hanzi Writer Data snapshot 68d10a4, updated from Make Me a Hanzi, 22 June 2019)
source.variation: The cited PRC-order dataset supplies eight ordered strokes for 性, in two pieces. Medians 1–3 draw the upright heart as 快 opens. Medians 4–8 draw 生 as 生 is written alone: a short left-falling stroke, a horizontal, a second horizontal, a vertical down through them, then a long horizontal along the foot. Make Me a Hanzi documents that its stroke paths are ordered in proper stroke order, its medians use the same coordinate system for stroke-order animation, and the project follows People's Republic of China stroke order. This learner path adapts those eight ordered medians to the vendored Noto Sans SC outline while preserving their order, their directions and seven intervening pen lifts; stroke widths and proportions differ between the Arphic-derived source graphics and Noto Sans SC.

source.variation: The cited PRC-order dataset supplies eight ordered strokes for 怪, in three pieces. Medians 1–3 draw the upright heart as 快 opens. Medians 4–5 draw 又: a horizontal that turns and falls to the left without lifting, then a long right-falling stroke. Medians 6–8 draw 土: a short horizontal, a vertical through it, then a long horizontal along the foot. Make Me a Hanzi documents that its stroke paths are ordered in proper stroke order, its medians use the same coordinate system for stroke-order animation, and the project follows People's Republic of China stroke order. This learner path adapts those eight ordered medians to the vendored Noto Sans SC outline while preserving their order, their directions, the turn and seven intervening pen lifts; stroke widths and proportions differ between the Arphic-derived source graphics and Noto Sans SC.

source.citation: Hanzi Writer Data 情.json, ordered stroke paths and medians 1–11 (Hanzi Writer Data snapshot 68d10a4, updated from Make Me a Hanzi, 22 June 2019)
source.variation: The cited PRC-order dataset supplies eleven ordered strokes for 情, in three pieces. Medians 1–3 draw the upright heart as 快 opens: a short dot on the left, a short dot on the right, then a long vertical between them. Medians 4–7 draw the upper right: two horizontals, a vertical down through them, then a long horizontal. Medians 8–11 draw 月 as 月 is written alone: a left side that curves to the lower left, a horizontal that turns down the right side and hooks to the left without lifting, then two short horizontals inside. Make Me a Hanzi documents that its stroke paths are ordered in proper stroke order, its medians use the same coordinate system for stroke-order animation, and the project follows People's Republic of China stroke order. This learner path adapts those eleven ordered medians to the vendored Noto Sans SC outline while preserving their order, their directions, the turn, the hook and ten intervening pen lifts; stroke widths and proportions differ between the Arphic-derived source graphics and Noto Sans SC.

source.citation: Hanzi Writer Data 想.json, ordered stroke paths and medians 1–13 (Hanzi Writer Data snapshot 68d10a4, updated from Make Me a Hanzi, 22 June 2019)
source.variation: The cited PRC-order dataset supplies thirteen ordered strokes for 想, in three pieces. Medians 1–4 draw 木 at the upper left: a horizontal, a vertical, a left-falling stroke and a dot. Medians 5–9 draw 目 beside it: its left side, the joined top and right side, two horizontals inside and the closing bottom. Medians 10–13 draw 心 under them: a dot, a curve that runs along the foot and hooks up without lifting, then two dots. Make Me a Hanzi documents that its stroke paths are ordered in proper stroke order, its medians use the same coordinate system for stroke-order animation, and the project follows People's Republic of China stroke order. This learner path adapts those thirteen ordered medians to the vendored Noto Sans SC outline while preserving their order, their directions, the turn, the hook and twelve intervening pen lifts; stroke widths and proportions differ between the Arphic-derived source graphics and Noto Sans SC.

source.citation: Hanzi Writer Data 意.json, ordered stroke paths and medians 1–13 (Hanzi Writer Data snapshot 68d10a4, updated from Make Me a Hanzi, 22 June 2019)
source.variation: The cited PRC-order dataset supplies thirteen ordered strokes for 意, in three pieces. Medians 1–5 draw 立 on top: a dot, a horizontal, two short strokes, then a long horizontal. Medians 6–9 draw 日 in the order the standalone character uses. Medians 10–13 draw 心 at the foot as 心 is written alone: a dot, a curve along the foot that hooks up without lifting, then two dots. Make Me a Hanzi documents that its stroke paths are ordered in proper stroke order, its medians use the same coordinate system for stroke-order animation, and the project follows People's Republic of China stroke order. This learner path adapts those thirteen ordered medians to the vendored Noto Sans SC outline while preserving their order, their directions, the turn, the hook and twelve intervening pen lifts; stroke widths and proportions differ between the Arphic-derived source graphics and Noto Sans SC.

source.citation: Hanzi Writer Data 感.json, ordered stroke paths and medians 1–13 (Hanzi Writer Data snapshot 68d10a4, updated from Make Me a Hanzi, 22 June 2019)
source.variation: The cited PRC-order dataset supplies thirteen ordered strokes for 感, in two pieces. Medians 1–9 draw the top: a long horizontal, a left-falling stroke down the left side, a short horizontal, a small 口 in the order the standalone character uses, then a long slanting stroke that hooks up at its foot without lifting, a left-falling stroke across it and a dot at the top right, as the right side of 钱 ends. Medians 10–13 draw 心 at the foot as 心 is written alone. Make Me a Hanzi documents that its stroke paths are ordered in proper stroke order, its medians use the same coordinate system for stroke-order animation, and the project follows People's Republic of China stroke order. This learner path adapts those thirteen ordered medians to the vendored Noto Sans SC outline while preserving their order, their directions, the turns, the hooks and twelve intervening pen lifts; stroke widths and proportions differ between the Arphic-derived source graphics and Noto Sans SC.

source.citation: Hanzi Writer Data 愿.json, ordered stroke paths and medians 1–14 (Hanzi Writer Data snapshot 68d10a4, updated from Make Me a Hanzi, 22 June 2019)
source.variation: The cited PRC-order dataset supplies fourteen ordered strokes for 愿, in four pieces. Medians 1–2 draw the cliff: a horizontal, then a long left-falling stroke from its left end. Medians 3–7 draw 白 as 白 is written alone. Medians 8–10 draw 小 as 小 is written alone: a vertical that hooks to the left, then a dot on each side. Medians 11–14 draw 心 as 心 is written alone: a dot, a curve along the foot that hooks up without lifting, then two dots. Make Me a Hanzi documents that its stroke paths are ordered in proper stroke order, its medians use the same coordinate system for stroke-order animation, and the project follows People's Republic of China stroke order. This learner path adapts those fourteen ordered medians to the vendored Noto Sans SC outline while preserving their order, their directions, the turn, the hooks and thirteen intervening pen lifts; stroke widths and proportions differ between the Arphic-derived source graphics and Noto Sans SC.

source.citation: Hanzi Writer Data 成.json, ordered stroke paths and medians 1–6 (Hanzi Writer Data snapshot 68d10a4, updated from Make Me a Hanzi, 22 June 2019)
source.variation: The cited PRC-order dataset supplies six ordered strokes for 成. Median 1 draws a horizontal from the left edge to past the middle; median 2 a long left-falling stroke from its left end; median 3 a short horizontal under it that turns down and hooks to the left without lifting; medians 4–6 a long slanting stroke from the top that hooks up at its foot without lifting, a short left-falling stroke across it, then a dot at the upper right, as the right side of 钱 ends. Make Me a Hanzi documents that its stroke paths are ordered in proper stroke order, its medians use the same coordinate system for stroke-order animation, and the project follows People's Republic of China stroke order. This learner path adapts those six ordered medians to the vendored Noto Sans SC outline while preserving their order, their directions, the turn, the hooks and five intervening pen lifts; stroke widths and proportions differ between the Arphic-derived source graphics and Noto Sans SC.

lift, then draw the top-right dot

source.citation: Hanzi Writer Data 我.json, ordered stroke paths and medians 1–7 (Hanzi Writer Data snapshot 68d10a4, updated from Make Me a Hanzi, 22 June 2019)
source.variation: The cited PRC-order dataset supplies seven ordered strokes for 我: an upper-left falling stroke, an upper horizontal, a hooked vertical, a lower rising stroke, a long curved slash that hooks upward on the right without lifting, a separate rising slash up-left, and a final upper-right dot. Make Me a Hanzi documents proper People's Republic of China stroke order and matching animation medians. This learner path adapts all seven medians to Noto Sans SC while preserving their order, directions, both joined hooks, and six lifts; Noto's long slash is more curved and its crossing strokes are more geometric than the Arphic-derived source graphics.

hook upward on the right without lifting
lift, then draw the separate rising slash up and left
lift, then place the upper-right dot down and right

source.citation: Hanzi Writer Data 手.json, ordered stroke paths and medians 1–4 (Hanzi Writer Data snapshot 68d10a4, updated from Make Me a Hanzi, 22 June 2019)
source.variation: The cited PRC-order dataset supplies four ordered strokes for 手. Median 1 draws a flat left-falling stroke across the top; medians 2–3 draw the two horizontals; median 4 draws the vertical last, from the top through all three, hooking to the left at its foot without lifting. Make Me a Hanzi documents that its stroke paths are ordered in proper stroke order, its medians use the same coordinate system for stroke-order animation, and the project follows People's Republic of China stroke order. This learner path adapts those four ordered medians to the vendored Noto Sans SC outline while preserving their order, their directions, the hook and three intervening pen lifts; stroke widths and proportions differ between the Arphic-derived source graphics and Noto Sans SC.

source.citation: Hanzi Writer Data 打.json, ordered stroke paths and medians 1–5 (Hanzi Writer Data snapshot 68d10a4, updated from Make Me a Hanzi, 22 June 2019)
source.variation: The cited PRC-order dataset supplies five ordered strokes for 打, in two pieces. Medians 1–3 draw the hand piece 扌 on the left: a horizontal, a vertical that hooks to the left at its foot without lifting, then a stroke that rises to the right across it. Medians 4–5 draw 丁 on the right: a horizontal, then a vertical that hooks to the left at its foot without lifting. Make Me a Hanzi documents that its stroke paths are ordered in proper stroke order, its medians use the same coordinate system for stroke-order animation, and the project follows People's Republic of China stroke order. This learner path adapts those five ordered medians to the vendored Noto Sans SC outline while preserving their order, their directions, the two hooks and four intervening pen lifts; stroke widths and proportions differ between the Arphic-derived source graphics and Noto Sans SC.

source.citation: Hanzi Writer Data 扫.json, ordered stroke paths and medians 1–6 (Hanzi Writer Data snapshot 68d10a4, updated from Make Me a Hanzi, 22 June 2019)
source.variation: The cited PRC-order dataset supplies six ordered strokes for 扫, in two pieces. Medians 1–3 draw the hand piece 扌 on the left as 打 opens: a horizontal, a vertical that hooks to the left at its foot without lifting, then a rising stroke. Medians 4–6 draw the right piece: a horizontal that turns down the right side without lifting, a middle horizontal, then the bottom horizontal. Make Me a Hanzi documents that its stroke paths are ordered in proper stroke order, its medians use the same coordinate system for stroke-order animation, and the project follows People's Republic of China stroke order. This learner path adapts those six ordered medians to the vendored Noto Sans SC outline while preserving their order, their directions, the hook, the turn and five intervening pen lifts; stroke widths and proportions differ between the Arphic-derived source graphics and Noto Sans SC. Noto's right side runs on below the bottom horizontal, where the source's stops above it.

source.variation: The cited PRC-order dataset supplies seven ordered strokes for 找, in two pieces. Medians 1–3 draw the hand piece on the left as 打 opens: a horizontal, a vertical that hooks to the left at its foot without lifting, then a stroke rising to the right across it. Medians 4–7 draw the right side: a horizontal, a long slanting stroke that hooks up at its foot without lifting, a left-falling stroke across it, then a dot at the top right. Make Me a Hanzi documents that its stroke paths are ordered in proper stroke order, its medians use the same coordinate system for stroke-order animation, and the project follows People's Republic of China stroke order. This learner path adapts those seven ordered medians to the vendored Noto Sans SC outline while preserving their order, their directions, the hooks and six intervening pen lifts; stroke widths and proportions differ between the Arphic-derived source graphics and Noto Sans SC.

Medians 1–3 draw the hand piece as 打 opens: a horizontal, a vertical that hooks to the left at the foot without lifting, then a rising stroke. Medians 4–7 draw 户 as 房 opens: a dot, a horizontal that turns down at its right end without lifting, a horizontal that closes it, then a long left-falling stroke down the left side. Make Me a Hanzi documents that its stroke paths are ordered in proper stroke order, its medians use the same coordinate system for stroke-order animation, and the project follows People's Republic of China stroke order. This learner path adapts those seven ordered medians to the vendored Noto Sans SC outline while preserving their order, their directions, the turn, the hook and six intervening pen lifts; stroke widths and proportions differ between the Arphic-derived source graphics and Noto Sans SC. Noto's 户 runs its right side on below the closing horizontal, where the source's stops above it.

source.variation: The cited PRC-order dataset supplies seven ordered strokes for 报, in two pieces. Medians 1–3 draw the hand piece as 打 opens. Medians 4–7 draw the right side: a horizontal that turns down and hooks to the left without lifting, a long vertical down its left side, then 又: a horizontal that turns and falls to the left without lifting, and a right-falling stroke. Make Me a Hanzi documents that its stroke paths are ordered in proper stroke order, its medians use the same coordinate system for stroke-order animation, and the project follows People's Republic of China stroke order. This learner path adapts those seven ordered medians to the vendored Noto Sans SC outline while preserving their order, their directions, the turns, the hooks and six intervening pen lifts; stroke widths and proportions differ between the Arphic-derived source graphics and Noto Sans SC.

source.citation: Hanzi Writer Data 救.json, ordered stroke paths and medians 1–11 (Hanzi Writer Data snapshot 68d10a4, updated from Make Me a Hanzi, 22 June 2019)
source.variation: The cited PRC-order dataset supplies eleven ordered strokes for 救, in two pieces. Medians 1–7 draw the left side: a horizontal, a vertical that hooks to the left at its foot without lifting, a dot and a rising stroke on its left, a short left-falling stroke and a short stroke on its right, then a dot at the upper right. Medians 8–11 draw the striking piece as 做 ends. Make Me a Hanzi documents that its stroke paths are ordered in proper stroke order, its medians use the same coordinate system for stroke-order animation, and the project follows People's Republic of China stroke order. This learner path adapts those eleven ordered medians to the vendored Noto Sans SC outline while preserving their order, their directions, the hook and ten intervening pen lifts; stroke widths and proportions differ between the Arphic-derived source graphics and Noto Sans SC.

source.citation: Hanzi Writer Data 教.json, ordered stroke paths and medians 1–11 (Hanzi Writer Data snapshot 68d10a4, updated from Make Me a Hanzi, 22 June 2019)
source.variation: The cited PRC-order dataset supplies eleven ordered strokes for 教, in two pieces. Medians 1–4 draw the top of 老 as 老 opens: a short horizontal, a vertical through it, a long horizontal, then a long left-falling stroke. Medians 5–7 draw 子 tucked under it: a horizontal that turns and falls to the left without lifting, a vertical that hooks to the left, then a stroke rising to the right. Medians 8–11 draw the striking piece as 做 ends. Make Me a Hanzi documents that its stroke paths are ordered in proper stroke order, its medians use the same coordinate system for stroke-order animation, and the project follows People's Republic of China stroke order. This learner path adapts those eleven ordered medians to the vendored Noto Sans SC outline while preserving their order, their directions, the turn, the hook and ten intervening pen lifts; stroke widths and proportions differ between the Arphic-derived source graphics and Noto Sans SC.

source.citation: Hanzi Writer Data 新.json, ordered stroke paths and medians 1–13 (Hanzi Writer Data snapshot 68d10a4, updated from Make Me a Hanzi, 22 June 2019)
source.variation: The cited PRC-order dataset supplies thirteen ordered strokes for 新, in three pieces. Medians 1–5 draw 立 on the upper left: a dot, a horizontal, two short strokes, then a horizontal along its foot. Medians 6–9 draw the tree piece under it: a horizontal, a vertical that hooks to the left at its foot without lifting, a left-falling stroke and a dot. Medians 10–13 draw the right side as 所 ends: a flat left-falling stroke, a long left-falling stroke that drops down, a horizontal and a long vertical. Make Me a Hanzi documents that its stroke paths are ordered in proper stroke order, its medians use the same coordinate system for stroke-order animation, and the project follows People's Republic of China stroke order. This learner path adapts those thirteen ordered medians to the vendored Noto Sans SC outline while preserving their order, their directions, the hook and twelve intervening pen lifts; stroke widths and proportions differ between the Arphic-derived source graphics and Noto Sans SC.

source.citation: Hanzi Writer Data 方.json, ordered stroke paths and medians 1–4 (Hanzi Writer Data snapshot 68d10a4, updated from Make Me a Hanzi, 22 June 2019)
source.variation: The cited PRC-order dataset supplies four ordered strokes for 方. Median 1 draws a dot on top; median 2 a long horizontal; median 3 a horizontal from under it that turns down and hooks to the left without lifting; median 4 a long left-falling stroke from under the horizontal. These are the last four strokes of 房. Make Me a Hanzi documents that its stroke paths are ordered in proper stroke order, its medians use the same coordinate system for stroke-order animation, and the project follows People's Republic of China stroke order. This learner path adapts those four ordered medians to the vendored Noto Sans SC outline while preserving their order, their directions, the turn, the hook and three intervening pen lifts; stroke widths and proportions differ between the Arphic-derived source graphics and Noto Sans SC.

source.citation: Hanzi Writer Data 旅.json, ordered stroke paths and medians 1–10 (Hanzi Writer Data snapshot 68d10a4, updated from Make Me a Hanzi, 22 June 2019)
source.variation: The cited PRC-order dataset supplies ten ordered strokes for 旅, in two pieces. Medians 1–4 draw the left piece: a dot, a horizontal, a short horizontal that turns down and hooks to the left without lifting, then a long left-falling stroke from under the horizontal. Medians 5–10 draw the right piece: a short left-falling stroke and a horizontal to its right, then a short left-falling stroke, a vertical that turns up to the right without lifting, another short left-falling stroke and a long right-falling stroke. Make Me a Hanzi documents that its stroke paths are ordered in proper stroke order, its medians use the same coordinate system for stroke-order animation, and the project follows People's Republic of China stroke order. This learner path adapts those ten ordered medians to the vendored Noto Sans SC outline while preserving their order, their directions, the turns, the hook and nine intervening pen lifts; stroke widths and proportions differ between the Arphic-derived source graphics and Noto Sans SC.

source.variation: The cited PRC-order dataset supplies four ordered strokes for 日. Make Me a Hanzi documents that its stroke paths are ordered in proper stroke order, its medians use the same coordinate system for stroke-order animation, and the project follows People's Republic of China stroke order. This learner path adapts those four ordered medians to the vendored Noto Sans SC outline while preserving their directions, the joined top-right corner, the inside-before-close order, and three intervening pen lifts; stroke widths and proportions differ between the Arphic-derived source graphics and Noto Sans SC.

source.citation: Hanzi Writer Data 早.json, ordered stroke paths and medians 1–6 (Hanzi Writer Data snapshot 68d10a4, updated from Make Me a Hanzi, 22 June 2019)
source.variation: The cited PRC-order dataset supplies six ordered strokes for 早. Medians 1–4 complete 日 first: the left side, a separately started top horizontal that turns down the right side without lifting, the middle horizontal, and the separately closing bottom horizontal. Median 5 then draws 十's horizontal left-to-right, and median 6 separately descends its vertical through the horizontal. Make Me a Hanzi documents proper People's Republic of China stroke order and matching animation medians. This learner path adapts all six medians to Noto Sans SC while preserving the complete 日-before-十 component order, the joined top-right turn, and five intervening lifts; Noto's 日 is squarer and 十's horizontal is flatter than the Arphic-derived source graphic.

source.citation: Hanzi Writer Data 时.json, ordered stroke paths and medians 1–7 (Hanzi Writer Data snapshot 68d10a4, updated from Make Me a Hanzi, 22 June 2019)
source.variation: The cited PRC-order dataset supplies seven ordered strokes for 时, in two pieces. Medians 1–4 draw 日 on the left as 日 is written alone. Medians 5–7 draw 寸 on the right as 对 ends: a horizontal, a vertical that hooks to the left at its foot without lifting, then a dot. Make Me a Hanzi documents that its stroke paths are ordered in proper stroke order, its medians use the same coordinate system for stroke-order animation, and the project follows People's Republic of China stroke order. This learner path adapts those seven ordered medians to the vendored Noto Sans SC outline while preserving their order, their directions, the turn, the hook and six intervening pen lifts; stroke widths and proportions differ between the Arphic-derived source graphics and Noto Sans SC.

source.variation: The cited PRC-order dataset supplies eight ordered strokes for 明, in two pieces. Medians 1–4 draw 日 on the left as 日 is written alone. Medians 5–8 draw 月 on the right: a vertical that curves to the lower left, a horizontal that turns down the right side and hooks to the left without lifting, then two horizontals inside. Make Me a Hanzi documents that its stroke paths are ordered in proper stroke order, its medians use the same coordinate system for stroke-order animation, and the project follows People's Republic of China stroke order. This learner path adapts those eight ordered medians to the vendored Noto Sans SC outline while preserving their order, their directions, the two turns, the hook and seven intervening pen lifts; stroke widths and proportions differ between the Arphic-derived source graphics and Noto Sans SC.

source.citation: Hanzi Writer Data 星.json, ordered stroke paths and medians 1–9 (Hanzi Writer Data snapshot 68d10a4, updated from Make Me a Hanzi, 22 June 2019)
source.variation: The cited PRC-order dataset supplies nine ordered strokes for 星, in two pieces. Medians 1–4 draw 日 on top as 日 is written alone: its left side, the joined top and right side, the middle horizontal, the closing bottom. Medians 5–9 draw 生 under it as 生 is written alone: a left-falling stroke, two horizontals, the vertical through them, then the long horizontal at the foot. Make Me a Hanzi documents that its stroke paths are ordered in proper stroke order, its medians use the same coordinate system for stroke-order animation, and the project follows People's Republic of China stroke order. This learner path adapts those nine ordered medians to the vendored Noto Sans SC outline while preserving their order, their directions, the turn and eight intervening pen lifts; stroke widths and proportions differ between the Arphic-derived source graphics and Noto Sans SC.

source.citation: Hanzi Writer Data 春.json, ordered stroke paths and medians 1–9 (Hanzi Writer Data snapshot 68d10a4, updated from Make Me a Hanzi, 22 June 2019)
source.variation: The cited PRC-order dataset supplies nine ordered strokes for 春, in two pieces. Medians 1–3 draw three horizontals, the lowest longest, as 三 is written; medians 4–5 draw the left-falling stroke through them and the right-falling stroke from the crossing, as 人 spreads; medians 6–9 draw 日 under them as 日 is written alone. Make Me a Hanzi documents that its stroke paths are ordered in proper stroke order, its medians use the same coordinate system for stroke-order animation, and the project follows People's Republic of China stroke order. This learner path adapts those nine ordered medians to the vendored Noto Sans SC outline while preserving their order, their directions, the turn and eight intervening pen lifts; stroke widths and proportions differ between the Arphic-derived source graphics and Noto Sans SC.

source.citation: Hanzi Writer Data 是.json, ordered stroke paths and medians 1–9 (Hanzi Writer Data snapshot 68d10a4, updated from Make Me a Hanzi, 22 June 2019)
source.variation: The cited PRC-order dataset supplies nine ordered strokes for 是. Medians 1–4 draw 日 first: its left vertical, joined top and right sides, inner horizontal, and closing bottom horizontal. Medians 5–9 then draw a wide horizontal, central vertical, short lower-right horizontal, lower-left falling stroke, and long finishing stroke down-right. Make Me a Hanzi documents proper People's Republic of China stroke order and matching animation medians. This learner path adapts all nine medians to Noto Sans SC while preserving their order, directions, the joined top-right corner, and eight intervening lifts; Noto's lower finishing stroke is broader and flatter than the Arphic-derived source graphic.

source.citation: Hanzi Writer Data 晚.json, ordered stroke paths and medians 1–11 (Hanzi Writer Data snapshot 68d10a4, updated from Make Me a Hanzi, 22 June 2019)
source.variation: The cited PRC-order dataset supplies eleven ordered strokes for 晚, in two pieces. Medians 1–4 draw 日 on the left as 日 is written alone. Medians 5–11 draw 免 on the right: a short left-falling stroke, a horizontal that turns to fall to the lower left without lifting, a box drawn as 口 is (its left side, the joined top and right side, the closing bottom), then the two strokes of 儿 from inside it: a left-falling stroke, and a vertical that bends right along the foot and hooks up without lifting. Make Me a Hanzi documents that its stroke paths are ordered in proper stroke order, its medians use the same coordinate system for stroke-order animation, and the project follows People's Republic of China stroke order. This learner path adapts those eleven ordered medians to the vendored Noto Sans SC outline while preserving their order, their directions, the turns, the hook and ten intervening pen lifts; stroke widths and proportions differ between the Arphic-derived source graphics and Noto Sans SC.

source.citation: Hanzi Writer Data 最.json, ordered stroke paths and medians 1–12 (Hanzi Writer Data snapshot 68d10a4, updated from Make Me a Hanzi, 22 June 2019)
source.variation: The cited PRC-order dataset supplies twelve ordered strokes for 最, in three pieces. Medians 1–4 draw 日 on top in the order the standalone character uses. Medians 5–10 draw the lower left: a long horizontal, two verticals, two short horizontals between them, then a stroke rising to the right at the foot. Medians 11–12 draw 又 on the lower right: a horizontal that turns and falls to the left without lifting, then a long right-falling stroke. Make Me a Hanzi documents that its stroke paths are ordered in proper stroke order, its medians use the same coordinate system for stroke-order animation, and the project follows People's Republic of China stroke order. This learner path adapts those twelve ordered medians to the vendored Noto Sans SC outline while preserving their order, their directions, the turns and eleven intervening pen lifts; stroke widths and proportions differ between the Arphic-derived source graphics and Noto Sans SC.

source.citation: Hanzi Writer Data 月.json, ordered stroke paths and medians 1–4 (Hanzi Writer Data snapshot 68d10a4, updated from Make Me a Hanzi, 22 June 2019)
source.variation: The cited PRC-order dataset supplies four ordered strokes for 月. Median 1 draws the left side, curving to the lower left; median 2 draws a horizontal that turns down the right side and hooks to the left without lifting; medians 3–4 draw the two horizontals inside. These are the strokes of 月 in 明, 期 and 前, in the same order. Make Me a Hanzi documents that its stroke paths are ordered in proper stroke order, its medians use the same coordinate system for stroke-order animation, and the project follows People's Republic of China stroke order. This learner path adapts those four ordered medians to the vendored Noto Sans SC outline while preserving their order, their directions, the turn, the hook and three intervening pen lifts; stroke widths and proportions differ between the Arphic-derived source graphics and Noto Sans SC.

source.citation: Hanzi Writer Data 有.json, ordered stroke paths and medians 1–6 (Hanzi Writer Data snapshot 68d10a4, updated from Make Me a Hanzi, 22 June 2019)
source.variation: The cited PRC-order dataset supplies six ordered strokes for 有. Medians 1–2 are the horizontal and the long left-falling stroke that cross at the top, in that order — horizontal before left-falling, the rule 大 and 六 already showed. Medians 3–6 build 月 beneath: left side, then the joined top-and-right that hooks at the base, then the two inner horizontals, so the enclosure is closed before it is filled. Make Me a Hanzi documents proper People's Republic of China stroke order and matching animation medians. This learner path adapts all six medians to Noto Sans SC while preserving their order, the joined corner, the base hook and five intervening lifts; Noto's 月 is slightly narrower than the source graphic.

source.citation: Hanzi Writer Data 望.json, ordered stroke paths and medians 1–11 (Hanzi Writer Data snapshot 68d10a4, updated from Make Me a Hanzi, 22 June 2019)
source.variation: The cited PRC-order dataset supplies eleven ordered strokes for 望, in three pieces. Medians 1–3 draw the upper left: a dot, a horizontal, then a short stroke down that turns right along the bottom without lifting. Medians 4–7 draw 月 as 月 is written alone. Medians 8–11 draw 王 as 王 is written alone: two horizontals, a vertical down through them, then a long horizontal along the foot. Make Me a Hanzi documents that its stroke paths are ordered in proper stroke order, its medians use the same coordinate system for stroke-order animation, and the project follows People's Republic of China stroke order. This learner path adapts those eleven ordered medians to the vendored Noto Sans SC outline while preserving their order, their directions, the turns, the hook and ten intervening pen lifts; stroke widths and proportions differ between the Arphic-derived source graphics and Noto Sans SC.

source.citation: Hanzi Writer Data 期.json, ordered stroke paths and medians 1–12 (Hanzi Writer Data snapshot 68d10a4, updated from Make Me a Hanzi, 22 June 2019)
source.variation: The cited PRC-order dataset supplies twelve ordered strokes for 期, in two pieces. Medians 1–8 draw 其 on the left: the top horizontal, the left and right verticals, the two horizontals between them, the long horizontal across their foot, then a left-falling stroke and a dot under it. Medians 9–12 draw 月 on the right: a vertical that curves to the lower left, a horizontal that turns down the right side and hooks to the left without lifting, then two horizontals inside. Make Me a Hanzi documents that its stroke paths are ordered in proper stroke order, its medians use the same coordinate system for stroke-order animation, and the project follows People's Republic of China stroke order. This learner path adapts those twelve ordered medians to the vendored Noto Sans SC outline while preserving their order, their directions, the turn, the hook and eleven intervening pen lifts; stroke widths and proportions differ between the Arphic-derived source graphics and Noto Sans SC.

source.citation: Hanzi Writer Data 本.json, ordered stroke paths and medians 1–5 (Hanzi Writer Data snapshot 68d10a4, updated from Make Me a Hanzi, 22 June 2019)
source.variation: The cited PRC-order dataset supplies five ordered strokes for 本. Medians 1–4 draw 木: a horizontal, a vertical, then the left-falling and right-falling strokes; median 5 draws a short horizontal across the vertical near its foot. Make Me a Hanzi documents that its stroke paths are ordered in proper stroke order, its medians use the same coordinate system for stroke-order animation, and the project follows People's Republic of China stroke order. This learner path adapts those five ordered medians to the vendored Noto Sans SC outline while preserving their order, their directions and four intervening pen lifts; stroke widths and proportions differ between the Arphic-derived source graphics and Noto Sans SC.

source.citation: Hanzi Writer Data 机.json, ordered stroke paths and medians 1–6 (Hanzi Writer Data snapshot 68d10a4, updated from Make Me a Hanzi, 22 June 2019)
source.variation: The cited PRC-order dataset supplies six ordered strokes for 机, in two pieces. Medians 1–4 draw 木 on the left as it opens 想: a horizontal, a vertical, a left-falling stroke and a dot. Medians 5–6 draw 几 on the right: a vertical that curves to the lower left, then a horizontal that turns down the right side, bends right along the foot and hooks up without lifting. Make Me a Hanzi documents that its stroke paths are ordered in proper stroke order, its medians use the same coordinate system for stroke-order animation, and the project follows People's Republic of China stroke order. This learner path adapts those six ordered medians to the vendored Noto Sans SC outline while preserving their order, their directions, the turns, the hook and five intervening pen lifts; stroke widths and proportions differ between the Arphic-derived source graphics and Noto Sans SC.

source.citation: Hanzi Writer Data 杯.json, ordered stroke paths and medians 1–8 (Hanzi Writer Data snapshot 68d10a4, updated from Make Me a Hanzi, 22 June 2019)
source.variation: The cited PRC-order dataset supplies eight ordered strokes for 杯, in two pieces. Medians 1–4 draw the tree piece on the left as 机 opens: a horizontal, a vertical, a left-falling stroke, then a dot. Medians 5–8 draw 不 on the right as 不 is written alone: a horizontal, a left-falling stroke, a vertical, then a dot. Make Me a Hanzi documents that its stroke paths are ordered in proper stroke order, its medians use the same coordinate system for stroke-order animation, and the project follows People's Republic of China stroke order. This learner path adapts those eight ordered medians to the vendored Noto Sans SC outline while preserving their order, their directions and seven intervening pen lifts; stroke widths and proportions differ between the Arphic-derived source graphics and Noto Sans SC.

source.variation: The cited PRC-order dataset supplies eight ordered strokes for 果, in two pieces. Medians 1–4 draw 日 on top in the order the standalone character uses. Medians 5–8 draw 木 under it: a horizontal, a vertical from the top of 日 down through everything to the foot, a left-falling and then a right-falling stroke. Make Me a Hanzi documents that its stroke paths are ordered in proper stroke order, its medians use the same coordinate system for stroke-order animation, and the project follows People's Republic of China stroke order. This learner path adapts those eight ordered medians to the vendored Noto Sans SC outline while preserving their order, their directions, the turn and seven intervening pen lifts; stroke widths and proportions differ between the Arphic-derived source graphics and Noto Sans SC.

Medians 7–9 draw 寸 as 对 ends: a horizontal, a vertical that hooks to the left without lifting, then a dot. Make Me a Hanzi documents that its stroke paths are ordered in proper stroke order, its medians use the same coordinate system for stroke-order animation, and the project follows People's Republic of China stroke order. This learner path adapts those nine ordered medians to the vendored Noto Sans SC outline while preserving their order, their directions, the turn, the hook and eight intervening pen lifts; stroke widths and proportions differ between the Arphic-derived source graphics and Noto Sans SC.

source.citation: Hanzi Writer Data 校.json, ordered stroke paths and medians 1–10 (Hanzi Writer Data snapshot 68d10a4, updated from Make Me a Hanzi, 22 June 2019)
source.variation: The cited PRC-order dataset supplies ten ordered strokes for 校, in two pieces. Medians 1–4 draw the tree piece on the left as 机 opens: a horizontal, a vertical, a left-falling stroke, then a dot. Medians 5–10 draw the right side: a dot and a horizontal, two short strokes under them leaning apart, then a long left-falling stroke and a long right-falling stroke crossing it. Make Me a Hanzi documents that its stroke paths are ordered in proper stroke order, its medians use the same coordinate system for stroke-order animation, and the project follows People's Republic of China stroke order. This learner path adapts those ten ordered medians to the vendored Noto Sans SC outline while preserving their order, their directions and nine intervening pen lifts; stroke widths and proportions differ between the Arphic-derived source graphics and Noto Sans SC.

source.citation: Hanzi Writer Data 欢.json, ordered stroke paths and medians 1–6 (Hanzi Writer Data snapshot 68d10a4, updated from Make Me a Hanzi, 22 June 2019)
source.variation: The cited PRC-order dataset supplies six ordered strokes for 欢. Medians 1–2 draw 又 exactly as 对 draws it, which is why the two characters are taught near each other; medians 3–6 draw 欠 as a short left-falling stroke, a hooked horizontal, then the long left-falling and right-falling pair that carry the whole right half. Make Me a Hanzi documents proper People's Republic of China stroke order and matching animation medians. This learner path adapts all six medians to Noto Sans SC while preserving their order, the internal turn in 又, the hook in 欠 and five intervening lifts; Noto's final right-falling stroke reaches further right than the Arphic-derived source graphic's.

source.citation: Hanzi Writer Data 歌.json, ordered stroke paths and medians 1–14 (Hanzi Writer Data snapshot 68d10a4, updated from Make Me a Hanzi, 22 June 2019)
source.variation: The cited PRC-order dataset supplies fourteen ordered strokes for 歌, in two pieces. Medians 1–10 draw 可 twice, as 可 is written alone: the upper one small, its vertical unhooked, then the lower one wide, its vertical hooking to the left without lifting. Medians 11–14 draw the right side: a short left-falling stroke, a horizontal that turns down to the left without lifting, a long left-falling stroke, then a long right-falling stroke. Make Me a Hanzi documents that its stroke paths are ordered in proper stroke order, its medians use the same coordinate system for stroke-order animation, and the project follows People's Republic of China stroke order. This learner path adapts those fourteen ordered medians to the vendored Noto Sans SC outline while preserving their order, their directions, the turns, the hook and thirteen intervening pen lifts; stroke widths and proportions differ between the Arphic-derived source graphics and Noto Sans SC.

source.citation: Hanzi Writer Data 法.json, ordered stroke paths and medians 1–8 (Hanzi Writer Data snapshot 68d10a4, updated from Make Me a Hanzi, 22 June 2019)
source.variation: The cited PRC-order dataset supplies eight ordered strokes for 法, in two pieces. Medians 1–3 draw the water piece as 洗 opens. Medians 4–8 draw 去 as 去 is written alone: a short horizontal, a vertical through it, a long horizontal, then a stroke that falls to the left and turns right without lifting, and a dot. Make Me a Hanzi documents that its stroke paths are ordered in proper stroke order, its medians use the same coordinate system for stroke-order animation, and the project follows People's Republic of China stroke order. This learner path adapts those eight ordered medians to the vendored Noto Sans SC outline while preserving their order, their directions, the turn and seven intervening pen lifts; stroke widths and proportions differ between the Arphic-derived source graphics and Noto Sans SC.

source.variation: The cited PRC-order dataset supplies nine ordered strokes for 洗, in two pieces. Medians 1–3 draw the water piece 氵 as 汉 opens: two dots, then a rising stroke. Medians 4–9 draw 先 on the right: a short left-falling stroke, a short horizontal, the vertical through it, the long horizontal, then 儿: a left-falling stroke and a vertical that bends right along the foot and hooks up without lifting. Make Me a Hanzi documents that its stroke paths are ordered in proper stroke order, its medians use the same coordinate system for stroke-order animation, and the project follows People's Republic of China stroke order. This learner path adapts those nine ordered medians to the vendored Noto Sans SC outline while preserving their order, their directions, the hook and eight intervening pen lifts; stroke widths and proportions differ between the Arphic-derived source graphics and Noto Sans SC.

source.citation: Hanzi Writer Data 海.json, ordered stroke paths and medians 1–10 (Hanzi Writer Data snapshot 68d10a4, updated from Make Me a Hanzi, 22 June 2019)
source.variation: The cited PRC-order dataset supplies ten ordered strokes for 海, in two pieces. Medians 1–3 draw the water piece as 洗 opens. Medians 4–10 draw 每 as 每 is written alone: a short left-falling stroke and a short horizontal, a stroke down the left side that turns right along the foot without lifting, a horizontal that turns down the right side and hooks to the left without lifting, a dot, a long horizontal out past both sides, then a dot under it. Make Me a Hanzi documents that its stroke paths are ordered in proper stroke order, its medians use the same coordinate system for stroke-order animation, and the project follows People's Republic of China stroke order. This learner path adapts those ten ordered medians to the vendored Noto Sans SC outline while preserving their order, their directions, the turns, the hook and nine intervening pen lifts; stroke widths and proportions differ between the Arphic-derived source graphics and Noto Sans SC.

source.citation: Hanzi Writer Data 游.json, ordered stroke paths and medians 1–12 (Hanzi Writer Data snapshot 68d10a4, updated from Make Me a Hanzi, 22 June 2019)
source.variation: The cited PRC-order dataset supplies twelve ordered strokes for 游, in three pieces. Medians 1–3 draw the water piece as 洗 opens: two dots, then a rising stroke. Medians 4–7 draw 方 as 房 ends: a dot, a long horizontal, a horizontal that turns down and hooks to the left without lifting, then a left-falling stroke. Medians 8–12 draw the right piece: a short left-falling stroke and a short horizontal, then 子 as 子 is written alone: a horizontal that turns and falls to the left without lifting, a vertical that hooks to the left, then a horizontal across. Make Me a Hanzi documents that its stroke paths are ordered in proper stroke order, its medians use the same coordinate system for stroke-order animation, and the project follows People's Republic of China stroke order. This learner path adapts those twelve ordered medians to the vendored Noto Sans SC outline while preserving their order, their directions, the turns, the hooks and eleven intervening pen lifts; stroke widths and proportions differ between the Arphic-derived source graphics and Noto Sans SC.

source.citation: Hanzi Writer Data 热.json, ordered stroke paths and medians 1–10 (Hanzi Writer Data snapshot 68d10a4, updated from Make Me a Hanzi, 22 June 2019)
source.variation: The cited PRC-order dataset supplies ten ordered strokes for 热, in three pieces. Medians 1–3 draw the hand piece as 打 opens: a horizontal, a vertical that hooks to the left at its foot without lifting, then a stroke rising to the right across it. Medians 4–6 draw the upper right: a left-falling stroke, a horizontal that turns down, bends right and hooks up without lifting, then a dot inside. Medians 7–10 draw the four dots along the foot as 点 ends. Make Me a Hanzi documents that its stroke paths are ordered in proper stroke order, its medians use the same coordinate system for stroke-order animation, and the project follows People's Republic of China stroke order. This learner path adapts those ten ordered medians to the vendored Noto Sans SC outline while preserving their order, their directions, the turns, the hooks and nine intervening pen lifts; stroke widths and proportions differ between the Arphic-derived source graphics and Noto Sans SC.

source.variation: The cited PRC-order dataset supplies twelve ordered strokes for 然, in three pieces. Medians 1–4 draw the upper left: a left-falling stroke, a horizontal that turns and falls to the left without lifting, then two dots. Medians 5–8 draw the upper right: 大 (a horizontal, a left-falling and a right-falling stroke), then a dot at its upper right. Medians 9–12 draw the four dots along the foot as 点 ends. Make Me a Hanzi documents that its stroke paths are ordered in proper stroke order, its medians use the same coordinate system for stroke-order animation, and the project follows People's Republic of China stroke order. This learner path adapts those twelve ordered medians to the vendored Noto Sans SC outline while preserving their order, their directions, the turn and eleven intervening pen lifts; stroke widths and proportions differ between the Arphic-derived source graphics and Noto Sans SC.

source.variation: The cited PRC-order dataset supplies ten ordered strokes for 爱, in three pieces. Medians 1–4 draw the top: a flat left-falling stroke from the right, two dots, then a short left-falling stroke. Medians 5–6 draw the cover as 写 opens: a short left stroke, then a horizontal that hooks down to the left without lifting. Medians 7–10 draw the bottom: a horizontal, a long left-falling stroke from above it, then 又: a horizontal that turns and falls to the left without lifting, and a right-falling stroke. Make Me a Hanzi documents that its stroke paths are ordered in proper stroke order, its medians use the same coordinate system for stroke-order animation, and the project follows People's Republic of China stroke order. This learner path adapts those ten ordered medians to the vendored Noto Sans SC outline while preserving their order, their directions, the turns and nine intervening pen lifts; stroke widths and proportions differ between the Arphic-derived source graphics and Noto Sans SC.

source.variation: The cited PRC-order dataset supplies four ordered strokes for 父. Medians 1–2 draw a short left-falling stroke on the left and a dot on the right; medians 3–4 a long left-falling stroke, then a long right-falling stroke crossing it. Make Me a Hanzi documents that its stroke paths are ordered in proper stroke order, its medians use the same coordinate system for stroke-order animation, and the project follows People's Republic of China stroke order. This learner path adapts those four ordered medians to the vendored Noto Sans SC outline while preserving their order, their directions and three intervening pen lifts; stroke widths and proportions differ between the Arphic-derived source graphics and Noto Sans SC.

source.variation: The cited PRC-order dataset supplies four ordered strokes for 牙. Median 1 draws a short horizontal along the top; median 2 a short stroke down on the left that turns and runs right without lifting; median 3 a vertical from the top horizontal down through it that hooks to the left at the foot without lifting; median 4 a long left-falling stroke from the middle down to the lower left. Make Me a Hanzi documents that its stroke paths are ordered in proper stroke order, its medians use the same coordinate system for stroke-order animation, and the project follows People's Republic of China stroke order. This learner path adapts those four ordered medians to the vendored Noto Sans SC outline while preserving their order, their directions, the turn, the hook and three intervening pen lifts; stroke widths and proportions differ between the Arphic-derived source graphics and Noto Sans SC.

source.citation: Hanzi Writer Data 特.json, ordered stroke paths and medians 1–10 (Hanzi Writer Data snapshot 68d10a4, updated from Make Me a Hanzi, 22 June 2019)
source.variation: The cited PRC-order dataset supplies ten ordered strokes for 特, in two pieces. Medians 1–4 draw the cow piece on the left: a short left-falling stroke, a horizontal, a long vertical through it, then a stroke rising to the right at the foot. Medians 5–10 draw the right side: 土 (a short horizontal, a vertical through it, a long horizontal under them), then 寸 as 对 ends: a horizontal, a vertical that hooks to the left without lifting, then a dot. Make Me a Hanzi documents that its stroke paths are ordered in proper stroke order, its medians use the same coordinate system for stroke-order animation, and the project follows People's Republic of China stroke order. This learner path adapts those ten ordered medians to the vendored Noto Sans SC outline while preserving their order, their directions, the hook and nine intervening pen lifts; stroke widths and proportions differ between the Arphic-derived source graphics and Noto Sans SC.

source.citation: Hanzi Writer Data 王.json, ordered stroke paths and medians 1–4 (Hanzi Writer Data snapshot 68d10a4, updated from Make Me a Hanzi, 22 June 2019)
source.variation: The cited PRC-order dataset supplies four ordered strokes for 王. Medians 1–2 draw two horizontals, the upper one first; median 3 the vertical down through them; median 4 the long horizontal along the foot, which closes the vertical. The left piece of 现 is written the same way, its last stroke rising. Make Me a Hanzi documents that its stroke paths are ordered in proper stroke order, its medians use the same coordinate system for stroke-order animation, and the project follows People's Republic of China stroke order. This learner path adapts those four ordered medians to the vendored Noto Sans SC outline while preserving their order, their directions and three intervening pen lifts; stroke widths and proportions differ between the Arphic-derived source graphics and Noto Sans SC.

source.citation: Hanzi Writer Data 现.json, ordered stroke paths and medians 1–8 (Hanzi Writer Data snapshot 68d10a4, updated from Make Me a Hanzi, 22 June 2019)
source.variation: The cited PRC-order dataset supplies eight ordered strokes for 现, in two pieces. Medians 1–4 draw the narrow left piece: two horizontals, a vertical down through both, then a stroke rising to the right at the foot. Medians 5–8 draw 见 on the right as 见 is written alone: its left side, a horizontal that turns down the right side without lifting, a left-falling stroke, then a vertical that bends right along the foot and hooks up without lifting. Make Me a Hanzi documents that its stroke paths are ordered in proper stroke order, its medians use the same coordinate system for stroke-order animation, and the project follows People's Republic of China stroke order. This learner path adapts those eight ordered medians to the vendored Noto Sans SC outline while preserving their order, their directions, the turns, the hook and seven intervening pen lifts; stroke widths and proportions differ between the Arphic-derived source graphics and Noto Sans SC.

source.citation: Hanzi Writer Data 球.json, ordered stroke paths and medians 1–11 (Hanzi Writer Data snapshot 68d10a4, updated from Make Me a Hanzi, 22 June 2019)
source.variation: The cited PRC-order dataset supplies eleven ordered strokes for 球, in two pieces. Medians 1–4 draw the left piece as 理 opens: two horizontals, a vertical through them, then a rising stroke. Medians 5–11 draw the right side: a horizontal, a vertical down through it that hooks to the left without lifting, a dot and a rising stroke on the left, a short left-falling stroke and a long right-falling stroke on the right, then the small dot at the top right. Make Me a Hanzi documents that its stroke paths are ordered in proper stroke order, its medians use the same coordinate system for stroke-order animation, and the project follows People's Republic of China stroke order. This learner path adapts those eleven ordered medians to the vendored Noto Sans SC outline while preserving their order, their directions, the hook and ten intervening pen lifts; stroke widths and proportions differ between the Arphic-derived source graphics and Noto Sans SC.

source.citation: Hanzi Writer Data 理.json, ordered stroke paths and medians 1–11 (Hanzi Writer Data snapshot 68d10a4, updated from Make Me a Hanzi, 22 June 2019)
source.variation: The cited PRC-order dataset supplies eleven ordered strokes for 理, in two pieces. Medians 1–4 draw the left piece as 现 opens: two horizontals, a vertical through them, then a stroke rising to the right. Medians 5–11 draw 里 as 里 is written alone. Make Me a Hanzi documents that its stroke paths are ordered in proper stroke order, its medians use the same coordinate system for stroke-order animation, and the project follows People's Republic of China stroke order. This learner path adapts those eleven ordered medians to the vendored Noto Sans SC outline while preserving their order, their directions, the turn and ten intervening pen lifts; stroke widths and proportions differ between the Arphic-derived source graphics and Noto Sans SC.

source.citation: Hanzi Writer Data 用.json, ordered stroke paths and medians 1–5 (Hanzi Writer Data snapshot 68d10a4, updated from Make Me a Hanzi, 22 June 2019)
source.variation: The cited PRC-order dataset supplies five ordered strokes for 用. Medians 1–2 draw the frame as 月 draws it: a left side that curves to the lower left, then a horizontal that turns down the right side and hooks to the left without lifting; medians 3–4 draw the two horizontals inside; median 5 draws the vertical down the middle last. Make Me a Hanzi documents that its stroke paths are ordered in proper stroke order, its medians use the same coordinate system for stroke-order animation, and the project follows People's Republic of China stroke order. This learner path adapts those five ordered medians to the vendored Noto Sans SC outline while preserving their order, their directions, the turn, the hook and four intervening pen lifts; stroke widths and proportions differ between the Arphic-derived source graphics and Noto Sans SC.

source.citation: Hanzi Writer Data 电.json, ordered stroke paths and medians 1–5 (Hanzi Writer Data snapshot 68d10a4, updated from Make Me a Hanzi, 22 June 2019)
source.variation: The cited PRC-order dataset supplies five ordered strokes for 电. Medians 1–4 draw 日 as 日 is written alone: its left side, the joined top and right side, the middle horizontal, the closing bottom. Median 5 draws the vertical through the middle from above the box, bending right along the foot and hooking up without lifting. Make Me a Hanzi documents that its stroke paths are ordered in proper stroke order, its medians use the same coordinate system for stroke-order animation, and the project follows People's Republic of China stroke order. This learner path adapts those five ordered medians to the vendored Noto Sans SC outline while preserving their order, their directions, the turns, the hook and four intervening pen lifts; stroke widths and proportions differ between the Arphic-derived source graphics and Noto Sans SC.

source.citation: Hanzi Writer Data 男.json, ordered stroke paths and medians 1–7 (Hanzi Writer Data snapshot 68d10a4, updated from Make Me a Hanzi, 22 June 2019)
source.variation: The cited PRC-order dataset supplies seven ordered strokes for 男, in two pieces. Medians 1–5 draw 田 on top: its left side, a horizontal that turns down the right side without lifting, the middle horizontal, the middle vertical, then the horizontal that closes the box. Medians 6–7 draw 力 below: a horizontal that turns down and hooks to the left without lifting, then a long left-falling stroke through it. Make Me a Hanzi documents that its stroke paths are ordered in proper stroke order, its medians use the same coordinate system for stroke-order animation, and the project follows People's Republic of China stroke order. This learner path adapts those seven ordered medians to the vendored Noto Sans SC outline while preserving their order, their directions, the two turns, the hook and six intervening pen lifts; stroke widths and proportions differ between the Arphic-derived source graphics and Noto Sans SC.

source.variation: The cited PRC-order dataset supplies eight ordered strokes for 画, in three pieces. Median 1 draws a horizontal on top. Medians 2–6 draw 田 as 男 opens: its left side, a horizontal that turns down the right side without lifting, the middle horizontal, the middle vertical, then the bottom. Medians 7–8 draw the open box: a stroke down the left side that turns right along the bottom without lifting, then a vertical on the right. Make Me a Hanzi documents that its stroke paths are ordered in proper stroke order, its medians use the same coordinate system for stroke-order animation, and the project follows People's Republic of China stroke order. This learner path adapts those eight ordered medians to the vendored Noto Sans SC outline while preserving their order, their directions, the turns and seven intervening pen lifts; stroke widths and proportions differ between the Arphic-derived source graphics and Noto Sans SC.

source.citation: Hanzi Writer Data 疼.json, ordered stroke paths and medians 1–10 (Hanzi Writer Data snapshot 68d10a4, updated from Make Me a Hanzi, 22 June 2019)
source.variation: The cited PRC-order dataset supplies ten ordered strokes for 疼, in two pieces. Medians 1–5 draw the sickness piece as 病 opens: a dot, a horizontal, a long left-falling stroke down the left side, then a dot and a rising stroke on the left. Medians 6–10 draw inside it a short left-falling stroke, a horizontal that turns and falls to the left without lifting, a long right-falling stroke, then two dots, one under the other. Make Me a Hanzi documents that its stroke paths are ordered in proper stroke order, its medians use the same coordinate system for stroke-order animation, and the project follows People's Republic of China stroke order. This learner path adapts those ten ordered medians to the vendored Noto Sans SC outline while preserving their order, their directions, the turn and nine intervening pen lifts; stroke widths and proportions differ between the Arphic-derived source graphics and Noto Sans SC.

source.variation: The cited PRC-order dataset supplies five ordered strokes for 白. Median 1 draws a short left-falling stroke at the top; medians 2–5 draw 日 under it as 日 is written alone: its left side, the joined top and right side, the middle horizontal, the closing bottom. Make Me a Hanzi documents that its stroke paths are ordered in proper stroke order, its medians use the same coordinate system for stroke-order animation, and the project follows People's Republic of China stroke order. This learner path adapts those five ordered medians to the vendored Noto Sans SC outline while preserving their order, their directions, the turn and four intervening pen lifts; stroke widths and proportions differ between the Arphic-derived source graphics and Noto Sans SC.

Median 1 is the bar across the very top; median 2 is the short left-falling stroke beneath it; medians 3–6 build the box below exactly as 四's outer frame and inner bar were built — left side, then the top-and-right turn, then the inner horizontal, then the closing floor. source.variation: The cited PRC-order dataset supplies eight ordered strokes for 的. Medians 1–5 draw 白: a short left-falling stroke, then the box built as 百's was — left side, joined top and right, inner bar, closing floor. Medians 6–8 draw 勺: a left-falling stroke, a long stroke down the right side that hooks left at the base, and a dot placed last inside the enclosure. Outside before inside, and the dot is the final stroke. Make Me a Hanzi documents proper People's Republic of China stroke order and matching animation medians. This learner path adapts all eight medians to the vendored Noto Sans SC outline while preserving their order, the two joined corners and seven intervening lifts; Noto's 勺 is narrower than the Arphic-derived source graphic.

source.variation: The cited PRC-order dataset supplies nine ordered strokes for 看. Medians 1–4 form the upper hand-like element; medians 5–9 complete 目 below. Make Me a Hanzi documents that its stroke paths are ordered in proper stroke order and that the project follows People's Republic of China stroke order. The ductus preserves that ordered sequence while fitting its learner pen paths to the vendored Noto Sans SC outline, whose width and proportions differ from the Arphic-derived source graphics.

source.citation: Hanzi Writer Data 真.json, ordered stroke paths and medians 1–10 (Hanzi Writer Data snapshot 68d10a4, updated from Make Me a Hanzi, 22 June 2019)
source.variation: The cited PRC-order dataset supplies ten ordered strokes for 真. Medians 1–2 draw 十 on top; medians 3–7 draw 目 under it as 想 writes it: its left side, a horizontal that turns down the right side without lifting, two horizontals inside and one closing the foot; median 8 draws a long horizontal under 目; medians 9–10 draw 八 at the foot. Make Me a Hanzi documents that its stroke paths are ordered in proper stroke order, its medians use the same coordinate system for stroke-order animation, and the project follows People's Republic of China stroke order. This learner path adapts those ten ordered medians to the vendored Noto Sans SC outline while preserving their order, their directions, the turn and nine intervening pen lifts; stroke widths and proportions differ between the Arphic-derived source graphics and Noto Sans SC.

source.citation: Hanzi Writer Data 眼.json, ordered stroke paths and medians 1–11 (Hanzi Writer Data snapshot 68d10a4, updated from Make Me a Hanzi, 22 June 2019)
source.variation: The cited PRC-order dataset supplies eleven ordered strokes for 眼, in two pieces. Medians 1–5 draw 目 as 想 writes it: its left side, a horizontal that turns down the right side without lifting, two horizontals inside, then the horizontal that closes the foot. Medians 6–11 draw the right side: a horizontal that turns down without lifting, two horizontals, a vertical down the left side that turns up to the right without lifting, a short left-falling stroke, then a long right-falling stroke. Make Me a Hanzi documents that its stroke paths are ordered in proper stroke order, its medians use the same coordinate system for stroke-order animation, and the project follows People's Republic of China stroke order. This learner path adapts those eleven ordered medians to the vendored Noto Sans SC outline while preserving their order, their directions, the turns and ten intervening pen lifts; stroke widths and proportions differ between the Arphic-derived source graphics and Noto Sans SC.

source.variation: The cited PRC-order dataset supplies seven ordered strokes for 社, in two pieces. Medians 1–4 draw the spirit piece as 祝 opens: a dot, a horizontal that turns and falls to the left without lifting, a vertical, then a short dot. Medians 5–7 draw 土: a short horizontal, a vertical through it, then a long horizontal along the foot. Make Me a Hanzi documents that its stroke paths are ordered in proper stroke order, its medians use the same coordinate system for stroke-order animation, and the project follows People's Republic of China stroke order. This learner path adapts those seven ordered medians to the vendored Noto Sans SC outline while preserving their order, their directions, the turn and six intervening pen lifts; stroke widths and proportions differ between the Arphic-derived source graphics and Noto Sans SC.

source.citation: Hanzi Writer Data 票.json, ordered stroke paths and medians 1–11 (Hanzi Writer Data snapshot 68d10a4, updated from Make Me a Hanzi, 22 June 2019)
source.variation: The cited PRC-order dataset supplies eleven ordered strokes for 票, in two pieces. Medians 1–6 draw the top piece: a horizontal, then a frame under it (its left side, a horizontal that turns down the right side without lifting, two short verticals inside, and the horizontal that closes it). Medians 7–11 draw the bottom piece: 二, a vertical that hooks to the left at its foot without lifting, then a short stroke falling to the left and a dot. Make Me a Hanzi documents that its stroke paths are ordered in proper stroke order, its medians use the same coordinate system for stroke-order animation, and the project follows People's Republic of China stroke order. This learner path adapts those eleven ordered medians to the vendored Noto Sans SC outline while preserving their order, their directions, the turn, the hook and ten intervening pen lifts; stroke widths and proportions differ between the Arphic-derived source graphics and Noto Sans SC.

source.citation: Hanzi Writer Data 离.json, ordered stroke paths and medians 1–10 (Hanzi Writer Data snapshot 68d10a4, updated from Make Me a Hanzi, 22 June 2019)
source.variation: The cited PRC-order dataset supplies ten ordered strokes for 离, in three pieces. Medians 1–2 draw a dot and a horizontal on top. Medians 3–6 draw the middle: a short left-falling stroke and a dot crossing it, then a box open at the top (a vertical that turns right along its foot without lifting, and a short vertical on the right). Medians 7–10 draw the foot: the frame's left side, a horizontal that turns down the right side and hooks to the left without lifting, then inside it a stroke that falls to the left and turns right without lifting, and a dot. Make Me a Hanzi documents that its stroke paths are ordered in proper stroke order, its medians use the same coordinate system for stroke-order animation, and the project follows People's Republic of China stroke order. This learner path adapts those ten ordered medians to the vendored Noto Sans SC outline while preserving their order, their directions, the turns, the hook and nine intervening pen lifts; stroke widths and proportions differ between the Arphic-derived source graphics and Noto Sans SC.

source.variation: The cited PRC-order dataset supplies nine ordered strokes for 秋, in two pieces. Medians 1–5 draw the grain piece on the left: a short left-falling stroke, a horizontal, a vertical down through it, a left-falling stroke from the crossing, then a dot. source.variation: The cited PRC-order dataset supplies nine ordered strokes for 突, in three pieces. Medians 1–3 draw the roof: a dot, a short stroke on the left, then a horizontal that hooks down at its right end without lifting. Medians 4–5 draw 八 under it: a left-falling stroke, then a stroke falling to the right. Medians 6–9 draw 大 at the foot, then a dot at its upper right. Make Me a Hanzi documents that its stroke paths are ordered in proper stroke order, its medians use the same coordinate system for stroke-order animation, and the project follows People's Republic of China stroke order. This learner path adapts those nine ordered medians to the vendored Noto Sans SC outline while preserving their order, their directions, the turn and eight intervening pen lifts; stroke widths and proportions differ between the Arphic-derived source graphics and Noto Sans SC. Noto's roof turns straight down at its right end, where the source's hooks to the left.

source.citation: Hanzi Writer Data 站.json, ordered stroke paths and medians 1–10 (Hanzi Writer Data snapshot 68d10a4, updated from Make Me a Hanzi, 22 June 2019)
source.variation: The cited PRC-order dataset supplies ten ordered strokes for 站, in two pieces. Medians 1–5 draw 立 on the left: a dot, a horizontal, a short stroke on each side, then a stroke rising to the right along the foot. Medians 6–10 draw 占 on the right as 点 opens: a vertical, a short horizontal to its right, then 口 in the order the standalone character uses. Make Me a Hanzi documents that its stroke paths are ordered in proper stroke order, its medians use the same coordinate system for stroke-order animation, and the project follows People's Republic of China stroke order. This learner path adapts those ten ordered medians to the vendored Noto Sans SC outline while preserving their order, their directions, the turn and nine intervening pen lifts; stroke widths and proportions differ between the Arphic-derived source graphics and Noto Sans SC.

source.variation: The cited PRC-order dataset supplies ten ordered strokes for 笑, in two pieces. Medians 1–6 draw the bamboo piece on top, the left half first: a short left-falling stroke, a short horizontal to the right from it, and a dot under the horizontal, then the same three on the right. Medians 7–10 draw the lower piece: a flat left-falling stroke across its top, then 大 as 大 is written alone: a horizontal, a left-falling and a right-falling stroke. Make Me a Hanzi documents that its stroke paths are ordered in proper stroke order, its medians use the same coordinate system for stroke-order animation, and the project follows People's Republic of China stroke order. This learner path adapts those ten ordered medians to the vendored Noto Sans SC outline while preserving their order, their directions and nine intervening pen lifts; stroke widths and proportions differ between the Arphic-derived source graphics and Noto Sans SC.

This learner path adapts those eleven ordered medians to the vendored Noto Sans SC outline while preserving their order, their directions, the turns, the hook and ten intervening pen lifts; stroke widths and proportions differ between the Arphic-derived source graphics and Noto Sans SC.

source.citation: Hanzi Writer Data 米.json, ordered stroke paths and medians 1–6 (Hanzi Writer Data snapshot 68d10a4, updated from Make Me a Hanzi, 22 June 2019)
source.variation: The cited PRC-order dataset supplies six ordered strokes for 米. Medians 1–2 draw the two short strokes above, the left one first; medians 3–4 draw the horizontal and the vertical down through it; medians 5–6 draw a left-falling and then a right-falling stroke from the crossing. Make Me a Hanzi documents that its stroke paths are ordered in proper stroke order, its medians use the same coordinate system for stroke-order animation, and the project follows People's Republic of China stroke order. This learner path adapts those six ordered medians to the vendored Noto Sans SC outline while preserving their order, their directions and five intervening pen lifts; stroke widths and proportions differ between the Arphic-derived source graphics and Noto Sans SC.

source.citation: Hanzi Writer Data 紧.json, ordered stroke paths and medians 1–10 (Hanzi Writer Data snapshot 68d10a4, updated from Make Me a Hanzi, 22 June 2019)
source.variation: The cited PRC-order dataset supplies ten ordered strokes for 紧, in three pieces. Medians 1–4 draw the top: two short verticals, then 又: a horizontal that turns and falls to the left without lifting, and a right-falling stroke. Medians 5–7 draw the middle: a stroke that falls to the left and turns right without lifting, a second one like it, then a dot. Medians 8–10 draw 小 as 小 is written alone: a vertical that hooks to the left, then a dot on each side. Make Me a Hanzi documents that its stroke paths are ordered in proper stroke order, its medians use the same coordinate system for stroke-order animation, and the project follows People's Republic of China stroke order. This learner path adapts those ten ordered medians to the vendored Noto Sans SC outline while preserving their order, their directions, the turns, the hook and nine intervening pen lifts; stroke widths and proportions differ between the Arphic-derived source graphics and Noto Sans SC.

source.citation: Hanzi Writer Data 老.json, ordered stroke paths and medians 1–6 (Hanzi Writer Data snapshot 68d10a4, updated from Make Me a Hanzi, 22 June 2019)
source.variation: The cited PRC-order dataset supplies six ordered strokes for 老, in two pieces. Medians 1–4 draw the top: a short horizontal, a vertical down through it, a long horizontal, then a long left-falling stroke from the upper right down through it to the lower left. Medians 5–6 draw the right half of 比 under it: a short left-falling stroke, then a vertical that bends right along the foot and hooks up without lifting. Make Me a Hanzi documents that its stroke paths are ordered in proper stroke order, its medians use the same coordinate system for stroke-order animation, and the project follows People's Republic of China stroke order. This learner path adapts those six ordered medians to the vendored Noto Sans SC outline while preserving their order, their directions, the turn, the hook and five intervening pen lifts; stroke widths and proportions differ between the Arphic-derived source graphics and Noto Sans SC.
