Make Me a Hanzi documents that its stroke paths are ordered in proper stroke order, its medians use the same coordinate system for stroke-order animation, and the project follows People's Republic of China stroke order. This learner path adapts those eleven ordered medians to the vendored Noto Sans SC outline while preserving their order, their directions, the turn and ten intervening pen lifts; stroke widths and proportions differ between the Arphic-derived source graphics and Noto Sans SC.

source.citation: Hanzi Writer Data 能.json, ordered stroke paths and medians 1–10 (Hanzi Writer Data snapshot 68d10a4, updated from Make Me a Hanzi, 22 June 2019)
source.variation: The cited PRC-order dataset supplies ten ordered strokes for 能, in two pieces. Medians 1–6 draw the left side: 厶 (a stroke that falls to the left and turns right without lifting, then a dot), then 月 under it (its left side, a horizontal that turns down the right side and hooks to the left without lifting, two horizontals inside). Medians 7–10 draw the two 匕 on the right, upper then lower, each a left-falling stroke then a vertical that bends right along its foot and hooks up without lifting. Make Me a Hanzi documents that its stroke paths are ordered in proper stroke order, its medians use the same coordinate system for stroke-order animation, and the project follows People's Republic of China stroke order. This learner path adapts those ten ordered medians to the vendored Noto Sans SC outline while preserving their order, their directions, the turns, the three hooks and nine intervening pen lifts; stroke widths and proportions differ between the Arphic-derived source graphics and Noto Sans SC.

source.variation: The cited PRC-order dataset supplies fourteen ordered strokes for 舞, in three pieces. Medians 1–8 draw the top: a short left-falling stroke, a short horizontal, a longer horizontal under it, four short verticals from left to right, then a long horizontal across the whole width. Medians 9–11 draw 夕 as 外 opens: a left-falling stroke, a horizontal that turns and falls to the left without lifting, then a dot. Medians 12–14 draw the lower right: a horizontal, a short stroke that drops and turns right without lifting, then a long vertical down through them. Make Me a Hanzi documents that its stroke paths are ordered in proper stroke order, its medians use the same coordinate system for stroke-order animation, and the project follows People's Republic of China stroke order. This learner path adapts those fourteen ordered medians to the vendored Noto Sans SC outline while preserving their order, their directions, the turns and thirteen intervening pen lifts; stroke widths and proportions differ between the Arphic-derived source graphics and Noto Sans SC.

source.citation: Hanzi Writer Data 船.json, ordered stroke paths and medians 1–11 (Hanzi Writer Data snapshot 68d10a4, updated from Make Me a Hanzi, 22 June 2019)
source.variation: The cited PRC-order dataset supplies eleven ordered strokes for 船, in two pieces. Medians 1–6 draw the boat piece on the left: a short left-falling stroke, a long left side that falls to the left at the foot, a horizontal that turns down the right side and hooks to the left without lifting, a dot, a horizontal rising to the right across the middle, then a dot under it. Medians 7–11 draw the right piece: a left-falling stroke and a horizontal that turns down and bends right without lifting, then 口 under them. Make Me a Hanzi documents that its stroke paths are ordered in proper stroke order, its medians use the same coordinate system for stroke-order animation, and the project follows People's Republic of China stroke order. source.variation: The cited PRC-order dataset supplies six ordered strokes for 色, in two pieces. Medians 1–2 draw the top: a short left-falling stroke, then a small horizontal that turns and falls to the left without lifting. Medians 3–6 draw the bottom: a horizontal that turns down the right side without lifting, a short vertical in the middle, a horizontal across under them, then a stroke down the left side that bends right along the foot and hooks up without lifting. Make Me a Hanzi documents that its stroke paths are ordered in proper stroke order, its medians use the same coordinate system for stroke-order animation, and the project follows People's Republic of China stroke order. This learner path adapts those six ordered medians to the vendored Noto Sans SC outline while preserving their order, their directions, the turns, the hook and five intervening pen lifts; stroke widths and proportions differ between the Arphic-derived source graphics and Noto Sans SC. Noto draws the first left-falling stroke long, on down past the turned stroke under it.

source.variation: The cited PRC-order dataset supplies seven ordered strokes for 花, in three pieces. Medians 1–3 draw 艹 on top as 菜 opens: a horizontal, then two short verticals through it. Medians 4–5 draw the person piece under it on the left: a left-falling stroke, then a vertical. Medians 6–7 draw the right side as the right half of 比: a left-falling stroke, then a vertical that bends right along the foot and hooks up without lifting. Make Me a Hanzi documents that its stroke paths are ordered in proper stroke order, its medians use the same coordinate system for stroke-order animation, and the project follows People's Republic of China stroke order. This learner path adapts those seven ordered medians to the vendored Noto Sans SC outline while preserving their order, their directions, the turn, the hook and six intervening pen lifts; stroke widths and proportions differ between the Arphic-derived source graphics and Noto Sans SC.

source.citation: Hanzi Writer Data 草.json, ordered stroke paths and medians 1–9 (Hanzi Writer Data snapshot 68d10a4, updated from Make Me a Hanzi, 22 June 2019)
source.variation: The cited PRC-order dataset supplies nine ordered strokes for 草, in two pieces. Medians 1–3 draw 艹 on top as 菜 opens: a horizontal, then two short verticals through it. Medians 4–9 draw 早 under it as 早 is written alone: 日, a long horizontal, then a vertical down from 日 through it. Make Me a Hanzi documents that its stroke paths are ordered in proper stroke order, its medians use the same coordinate system for stroke-order animation, and the project follows People's Republic of China stroke order. This learner path adapts those nine ordered medians to the vendored Noto Sans SC outline while preserving their order, their directions, the turn and eight intervening pen lifts; stroke widths and proportions differ between the Arphic-derived source graphics and Noto Sans SC.

source.citation: Hanzi Writer Data 菜.json, ordered stroke paths and medians 1–11 (Hanzi Writer Data snapshot 68d10a4, updated from Make Me a Hanzi, 22 June 2019)
source.variation: The cited PRC-order dataset supplies eleven ordered strokes for 菜, in three pieces. Medians 1–3 draw the grass piece 艹: a horizontal, then two short verticals through it. Medians 4–7 draw 爫 under it: a flat left-falling stroke, two dots and a short left-falling stroke. Medians 8–11 draw 木 at the foot: a horizontal, a vertical, then the left-falling and right-falling strokes. Make Me a Hanzi documents that its stroke paths are ordered in proper stroke order, its medians use the same coordinate system for stroke-order animation, and the project follows People's Republic of China stroke order. This learner path adapts those eleven ordered medians to the vendored Noto Sans SC outline while preserving their order, their directions and ten intervening pen lifts; stroke widths and proportions differ between the Arphic-derived source graphics and Noto Sans SC.

source.citation: Hanzi Writer Data 虽.json, ordered stroke paths and medians 1–9 (Hanzi Writer Data snapshot 68d10a4, updated from Make Me a Hanzi, 22 June 2019)
source.variation: The cited PRC-order dataset supplies nine ordered strokes for 虽, in two pieces. Medians 1–3 draw 口 on top in the order the standalone character uses. Medians 4–9 draw the lower piece: a small box (its left side, a horizontal that turns down without lifting, the horizontal that closes it), a vertical down through it, a stroke rising to the right along the foot, then a dot on the right. Make Me a Hanzi documents that its stroke paths are ordered in proper stroke order, its medians use the same coordinate system for stroke-order animation, and the project follows People's Republic of China stroke order. This learner path adapts those nine ordered medians to the vendored Noto Sans SC outline while preserving their order, their directions, the turn and eight intervening pen lifts; stroke widths and proportions differ between the Arphic-derived source graphics and Noto Sans SC.

source.variation: The cited PRC-order dataset supplies six ordered strokes for 血, in two pieces. Median 1 draws a short left-falling stroke on top. Medians 2–6 draw the dish as 温 ends: a short vertical, a horizontal that turns down the right side without lifting, two short verticals inside, then a long horizontal under everything. Make Me a Hanzi documents that its stroke paths are ordered in proper stroke order, its medians use the same coordinate system for stroke-order animation, and the project follows People's Republic of China stroke order. This learner path adapts those six ordered medians to the vendored Noto Sans SC outline while preserving their order, their directions, the turn and five intervening pen lifts; stroke widths and proportions differ between the Arphic-derived source graphics and Noto Sans SC.

source.citation: Hanzi Writer Data 西.json, ordered stroke paths and medians 1–6 (Hanzi Writer Data snapshot 68d10a4, updated from Make Me a Hanzi, 22 June 2019)
source.variation: The cited PRC-order dataset supplies six ordered strokes for 西. Median 1 draws the top horizontal; medians 2–3 draw the box: its left side, then a horizontal that turns down the right side without lifting; medians 4–5 draw inside it, each from above the box, a left-falling stroke and a vertical that bends right without lifting; median 6 closes the box along the foot. Make Me a Hanzi documents that its stroke paths are ordered in proper stroke order, its medians use the same coordinate system for stroke-order animation, and the project follows People's Republic of China stroke order. This learner path adapts those six ordered medians to the vendored Noto Sans SC outline while preserving their order, their directions, the turns and five intervening pen lifts; stroke widths and proportions differ between the Arphic-derived source graphics and Noto Sans SC.

source.variation: The cited PRC-order dataset supplies nine ordered strokes for 要, in two pieces. Medians 1–6 draw 覀 on top: the top horizontal, the box's left side, its joined top and right side, the two short verticals inside, then the closing bottom. Medians 7–9 draw 女 under it as 女 is written alone: a stroke that falls to the left and turns down to the right without lifting, a left-falling stroke, then the long horizontal. Make Me a Hanzi documents that its stroke paths are ordered in proper stroke order, its medians use the same coordinate system for stroke-order animation, and the project follows People's Republic of China stroke order. This learner path adapts those nine ordered medians to the vendored Noto Sans SC outline while preserving their order, their directions, the turns and eight intervening pen lifts; stroke widths and proportions differ between the Arphic-derived source graphics and Noto Sans SC.

source.citation: Hanzi Writer Data 见.json, ordered stroke paths and medians 1–4 (Hanzi Writer Data snapshot 68d10a4, updated from Make Me a Hanzi, 22 June 2019)
source.variation: The cited PRC-order dataset supplies four ordered strokes for 见. Median 1 descends the frame's left side. Median 2 separately draws the top horizontal and turns down the right side without lifting. Median 3 draws the inner left-falling leg. Median 4 separately descends the second leg, bends right along the base, and finishes with an upward hook without lifting. Make Me a Hanzi documents proper People's Republic of China stroke order and matching animation medians. This learner path adapts all four medians to Noto Sans SC while preserving their order, the frame-before-legs sequence, all three joined turns across the top-right frame and vertical-bend hook, and three intervening lifts; Noto's upper frame is squarer and its hooked leg is flatter than the Arphic-derived source graphic.

source.citation: Hanzi Writer Data 觉.json, ordered stroke paths and medians 1–9 (Hanzi Writer Data snapshot 68d10a4, updated from Make Me a Hanzi, 22 June 2019)
source.variation: The cited PRC-order dataset supplies nine ordered strokes for 觉, in three pieces. Medians 1–3 draw the three short strokes on top, left to right: two dots, then a short left-falling stroke. Medians 4–5 draw the cover: a short stroke on the left, then a horizontal that hooks down to the left without lifting. Medians 6–9 draw 见 at the foot: its left side, a horizontal that turns down the right side without lifting, a left-falling stroke, then a vertical that bends right along the foot and hooks up without lifting. Make Me a Hanzi documents that its stroke paths are ordered in proper stroke order, its medians use the same coordinate system for stroke-order animation, and the project follows People's Republic of China stroke order. This learner path adapts those nine ordered medians to the vendored Noto Sans SC outline while preserving their order, their directions, the turns, the hooks and eight intervening pen lifts; stroke widths and proportions differ between the Arphic-derived source graphics and Noto Sans SC. Noto's cover turns straight down at its right end, where the source's hooks to the left.

source.citation: Hanzi Writer Data 解.json, ordered stroke paths and medians 1–13 (Hanzi Writer Data snapshot 68d10a4, updated from Make Me a Hanzi, 22 June 2019)
source.variation: The cited PRC-order dataset supplies thirteen ordered strokes for 解, in three pieces. Medians 1–7 draw 角 on the left: a short left-falling stroke, a horizontal that turns and falls to the left without lifting, a long left-falling stroke down the left side, a horizontal that turns down the right side and hooks to the left without lifting, two short horizontals inside, then a vertical down the middle. Medians 8–9 draw the upper right: a horizontal that turns down and hooks to the left without lifting, then a left-falling stroke inside it. Medians 10–13 draw the lower right as 午 is written: a short left-falling stroke, two horizontals and a vertical through them. Make Me a Hanzi documents that its stroke paths are ordered in proper stroke order, its medians use the same coordinate system for stroke-order animation, and the project follows People's Republic of China stroke order. This learner path adapts those thirteen ordered medians to the vendored Noto Sans SC outline while preserving their order, their directions, the turns, the hooks and twelve intervening pen lifts; stroke widths and proportions differ between the Arphic-derived source graphics and Noto Sans SC.

source.citation: Hanzi Writer Data 警.json, ordered stroke paths and medians 1–19 (Hanzi Writer Data snapshot 68d10a4, updated from Make Me a Hanzi, 22 June 2019)
source.variation: The cited PRC-order dataset supplies nineteen ordered strokes for 警, in three pieces. Medians 1–8 draw the upper left: 艹 as 菜 opens, a short left-falling stroke, a horizontal that turns down and hooks to the left without lifting, then a small 口 in the order the standalone character uses. Medians 9–12 draw the striking piece on the upper right as 做 ends. Medians 13–19 draw the foot: a dot, a long horizontal and two shorter ones, then 口. Make Me a Hanzi documents that its stroke paths are ordered in proper stroke order, its medians use the same coordinate system for stroke-order animation, and the project follows People's Republic of China stroke order. This learner path adapts those nineteen ordered medians to the vendored Noto Sans SC outline while preserving their order, their directions, the turns, the hook and eighteen intervening pen lifts; stroke widths and proportions differ between the Arphic-derived source graphics and Noto Sans SC.

source.citation: Hanzi Writer Data 讠.json, ordered stroke paths and medians 1–2 (Hanzi Writer Data snapshot 68d10a4, updated from Make Me a Hanzi, 22 June 2019)
source.variation: The cited PRC-order dataset supplies two ordered strokes for 讠. Median 1 starts at the upper left and draws the dot down-right; median 2 restarts at the left edge, rises slightly across the short horizontal, turns without lifting to descend, then turns again without lifting and finishes up-right. Make Me a Hanzi documents that its stroke paths are ordered in proper stroke order, its medians use the same coordinate system for stroke-order animation, and the project follows People's Republic of China stroke order. This learner path adapts those two ordered medians to the vendored Noto Sans SC outline while preserving their directions, both turns inside the second stroke, and one intervening pen lift; Noto's middle horizontal and descent are squarer than the source median, and stroke widths and proportions differ between the Arphic-derived source graphics and Noto Sans SC.

source.variation: The cited PRC-order dataset supplies eight ordered strokes for 话, in two pieces. Medians 1–2 draw the speech piece 讠 as 谢 opens. Medians 3–8 draw 舌 on the right: a flat left-falling stroke across the top, the long horizontal, a vertical down from the top stroke, then 口 under them in the order the standalone character uses. Make Me a Hanzi documents that its stroke paths are ordered in proper stroke order, its medians use the same coordinate system for stroke-order animation, and the project follows People's Republic of China stroke order. This learner path adapts those eight ordered medians to the vendored Noto Sans SC outline while preserving their order, their directions, the turns, the flick and seven intervening pen lifts; stroke widths and proportions differ between the Arphic-derived source graphics and Noto Sans SC.

Medians 1–2 draw the speech piece as 说 opens: a dot, then a short horizontal that turns down and flicks up to the right without lifting. Medians 3–8 draw the right side as 孩 ends: a dot, a horizontal, a stroke that falls to the left and turns up to the right without lifting, two left-falling strokes, then a dot. Make Me a Hanzi documents that its stroke paths are ordered in proper stroke order, its medians use the same coordinate system for stroke-order animation, and the project follows People's Republic of China stroke order. This learner path adapts those eight ordered medians to the vendored Noto Sans SC outline while preserving their order, their directions, the turns and seven intervening pen lifts; stroke widths and proportions differ between the Arphic-derived source graphics and Noto Sans SC.

source.citation: Hanzi Writer Data 说.json, ordered stroke paths and medians 1–9 (Hanzi Writer Data snapshot 68d10a4, updated from Make Me a Hanzi, 22 June 2019)
source.variation: The cited PRC-order dataset supplies nine ordered strokes for 说, in two pieces. Medians 1–2 draw the speech piece 讠 as 谢 opens: a dot, then a short horizontal that turns down and flicks up to the right without lifting. Medians 3–9 draw 兑 on the right: two short strokes spreading at the top, 口 in the order the standalone character uses, then 儿: a left-falling stroke and a vertical that bends right along the foot and hooks up without lifting. Make Me a Hanzi documents that its stroke paths are ordered in proper stroke order, its medians use the same coordinate system for stroke-order animation, and the project follows People's Republic of China stroke order. This learner path adapts those nine ordered medians to the vendored Noto Sans SC outline while preserving their order, their directions, the turns, the flick, the hook and eight intervening pen lifts; stroke widths and proportions differ between the Arphic-derived source graphics and Noto Sans SC.

source.variation: The cited PRC-order dataset supplies ten ordered strokes for 请. Medians 1–2 draw 讠: a down-right dot, then a separately started short horizontal that turns down and finishes up-right without lifting. Medians 3–10 draw 青: two upper horizontals, a central vertical, a wide middle horizontal, the lower left side, a separately started lower top horizontal that turns down the right side and hooks left at the base without lifting, then two inner horizontals. Make Me a Hanzi documents proper People's Republic of China stroke order and matching animation medians. This learner path adapts all ten medians to Noto Sans SC while preserving their order, all four internal turns across 讠 and 青, and nine intervening lifts; Noto's 青 horizontals are flatter and its lower enclosure is squarer than the Arphic-derived source graphic.

source.variation: The cited PRC-order dataset supplies ten ordered strokes for 读, in two pieces. Medians 1–2 draw the speech piece as 说 opens: a dot, then a short horizontal that turns down and flicks up to the right without lifting. Medians 3–10 draw the right side: 十 (a horizontal and a vertical through it), then 买 as 买 is written alone: a horizontal that hooks down to the left without lifting, two dots, a long horizontal, a left-falling stroke through it, and a dot. Make Me a Hanzi documents that its stroke paths are ordered in proper stroke order, its medians use the same coordinate system for stroke-order animation, and the project follows People's Republic of China stroke order. This learner path adapts those ten ordered medians to the vendored Noto Sans SC outline while preserving their order, their directions, the turns, the hooks and nine intervening pen lifts; stroke widths and proportions differ between the Arphic-derived source graphics and Noto Sans SC.

source.citation: Hanzi Writer Data 谢.json, ordered stroke paths and medians 1–12 (Hanzi Writer Data snapshot 68d10a4, updated from Make Me a Hanzi, 22 June 2019)
source.variation: The cited PRC-order dataset supplies twelve ordered strokes for 谢. Medians 1–2 draw 讠: a down-right dot, then a separately started short horizontal that turns down and finishes up-right without lifting. Medians 3–9 draw 身: an upper falling stroke, the left side, a separately started top horizontal that turns down the right side and hooks left at the base without lifting, two inner horizontals, a wide lower horizontal, and a lower falling stroke down-left. Medians 10–12 draw 寸: a horizontal, a separately started vertical that hooks left at the base without lifting, and a final down-right dot. Make Me a Hanzi documents proper People's Republic of China stroke order and matching animation medians. This learner path adapts all twelve medians to Noto Sans SC while preserving their order, all five internal turns across 讠, 身, and 寸, and eleven intervening lifts; Noto's 身 enclosure is squarer and 寸's hook is flatter than the Arphic-derived source graphic.

source.citation: Hanzi Writer Data 赛.json, ordered stroke paths and medians 1–14 (Hanzi Writer Data snapshot 68d10a4, updated from Make Me a Hanzi, 22 June 2019)
source.variation: The cited PRC-order dataset supplies fourteen ordered strokes for 赛, in three pieces. Medians 1–3 draw the roof as 安 opens. Medians 4–10 draw the middle: two short horizontals, two verticals down through them, a long horizontal, then a left-falling and a right-falling stroke. Medians 11–14 draw the foot: a vertical, a horizontal that turns down the right side without lifting, a left-falling stroke inside, then a dot. Make Me a Hanzi documents that its stroke paths are ordered in proper stroke order, its medians use the same coordinate system for stroke-order animation, and the project follows People's Republic of China stroke order. This learner path adapts those fourteen ordered medians to the vendored Noto Sans SC outline while preserving their order, their directions, the turns and thirteen intervening pen lifts; stroke widths and proportions differ between the Arphic-derived source graphics and Noto Sans SC. Noto's roof turns straight down at its right end, where the source's hooks to the left.

source.variation: The cited PRC-order dataset supplies ten ordered strokes for 起, in two pieces. Medians 1–7 draw 走 on the left: a horizontal, a vertical through it, the long horizontal, a lower vertical, a short horizontal to its right, a left-falling stroke, then the long right-falling stroke along the foot. Medians 8–10 draw 己 on the right above that stroke: a horizontal that turns down without lifting, the middle horizontal, then a vertical that bends right along the foot and hooks up without lifting. Make Me a Hanzi documents that its stroke paths are ordered in proper stroke order, its medians use the same coordinate system for stroke-order animation, and the project follows People's Republic of China stroke order. This learner path adapts those ten ordered medians to the vendored Noto Sans SC outline while preserving their order, their directions, the turns, the hook and nine intervening pen lifts; stroke widths and proportions differ between the Arphic-derived source graphics and Noto Sans SC.

source.citation: Hanzi Writer Data 路.json, ordered stroke paths and medians 1–13 (Hanzi Writer Data snapshot 68d10a4, updated from Make Me a Hanzi, 22 June 2019)
source.variation: The cited PRC-order dataset supplies thirteen ordered strokes for 路, in two pieces. Medians 1–7 draw the foot piece on the left: 口 in the order the standalone character uses, then a short vertical under it, a short horizontal to its right, a short vertical on the left, and a stroke along the foot rising to the right. Medians 8–13 draw the right side: a short left-falling stroke, a horizontal that turns and falls to the left without lifting, a long right-falling stroke, then 口 under them. Make Me a Hanzi documents that its stroke paths are ordered in proper stroke order, its medians use the same coordinate system for stroke-order animation, and the project follows People's Republic of China stroke order. This learner path adapts those thirteen ordered medians to the vendored Noto Sans SC outline while preserving their order, their directions, the turns and twelve intervening pen lifts; stroke widths and proportions differ between the Arphic-derived source graphics and Noto Sans SC.

source.citation: Hanzi Writer Data 身.json, ordered stroke paths and medians 1–7 (Hanzi Writer Data snapshot 68d10a4, updated from Make Me a Hanzi, 22 June 2019)
source.variation: The cited PRC-order dataset supplies seven ordered strokes for 身. Median 1 draws a short left-falling stroke on top; medians 2–3 draw the frame: a short left side, then a horizontal that turns down the right side and hooks to the left at the foot without lifting; medians 4–5 draw two short horizontals inside; median 6 draws a stroke rising from the far left across the frame; median 7 draws a long left-falling stroke from the upper right to the lower left. Make Me a Hanzi documents that its stroke paths are ordered in proper stroke order, its medians use the same coordinate system for stroke-order animation, and the project follows People's Republic of China stroke order. This learner path adapts those seven ordered medians to the vendored Noto Sans SC outline while preserving their order, their directions, the turn, the hook and six intervening pen lifts; stroke widths and proportions differ between the Arphic-derived source graphics and Noto Sans SC. Noto's rising stroke lies almost level.

source.citation: Hanzi Writer Data 车.json, ordered stroke paths and medians 1–4 (Hanzi Writer Data snapshot 68d10a4, updated from Make Me a Hanzi, 22 June 2019)
source.variation: The cited PRC-order dataset supplies four ordered strokes for 车. Median 1 draws the top horizontal; median 2 draws a stroke that falls to the lower left and turns right across the middle without lifting; median 3 draws the long bottom horizontal; median 4 draws the vertical last, from the middle down through it. Make Me a Hanzi documents that its stroke paths are ordered in proper stroke order, its medians use the same coordinate system for stroke-order animation, and the project follows People's Republic of China stroke order. This learner path adapts those four ordered medians to the vendored Noto Sans SC outline while preserving their order, their directions, the turn and three intervening pen lifts; stroke widths and proportions differ between the Arphic-derived source graphics and Noto Sans SC.

source.variation: The cited PRC-order dataset supplies five ordered strokes for 边, in two pieces, the walking piece written last. Medians 1–2 draw 力 as 男 ends: a horizontal that turns down and hooks to the left without lifting, then a long left-falling stroke through it. Medians 3–5 draw 辶 as 这 closes: a dot, a stroke that runs right, turns down, turns again and falls to the left without lifting, then the long flat right-falling stroke along the foot. Make Me a Hanzi documents that its stroke paths are ordered in proper stroke order, its medians use the same coordinate system for stroke-order animation, and the project follows People's Republic of China stroke order. This learner path adapts those five ordered medians to the vendored Noto Sans SC outline while preserving their order, their directions, the turns, the hook and four intervening pen lifts; stroke widths and proportions differ between the Arphic-derived source graphics and Noto Sans SC.

Make Me a Hanzi documents that its stroke paths are ordered in proper stroke order, its medians use the same coordinate system for stroke-order animation, and the project follows People's Republic of China stroke order. This learner path adapts those seven ordered medians to the vendored Noto Sans SC outline while preserving their order, their directions, the turns and six intervening pen lifts; stroke widths and proportions differ between the Arphic-derived source graphics and Noto Sans SC.

source.variation: The cited PRC-order dataset supplies nine ordered strokes for 送, in two pieces, the walking piece written last. Medians 1–6 draw 关 as 关 is written alone, its last stroke shortened to a dot. Medians 7–9 draw 辶 as 这 closes: a dot, a stroke that runs right, turns down, turns again and falls to the left without lifting, then the long flat right-falling stroke along the foot. Make Me a Hanzi documents that its stroke paths are ordered in proper stroke order, its medians use the same coordinate system for stroke-order animation, and the project follows People's Republic of China stroke order. This learner path adapts those nine ordered medians to the vendored Noto Sans SC outline while preserving their order, their directions, the turns and eight intervening pen lifts; stroke widths and proportions differ between the Arphic-derived source graphics and Noto Sans SC.

source.citation: Hanzi Writer Data 速.json, ordered stroke paths and medians 1–10 (Hanzi Writer Data snapshot 68d10a4, updated from Make Me a Hanzi, 22 June 2019)
source.variation: The cited PRC-order dataset supplies ten ordered strokes for 速, in two pieces, the walking piece written last. Medians 1–7 draw the upper piece: a horizontal, 口 under it, a long vertical down through both, then a left-falling stroke and a dot from the vertical, as at the foot of 木. Medians 8–10 draw 辶 as 这 ends: a dot, a stroke that runs right, turns down, turns again and falls to the left without lifting, then the long flat right-falling stroke along the foot. Make Me a Hanzi documents that its stroke paths are ordered in proper stroke order, its medians use the same coordinate system for stroke-order animation, and the project follows People's Republic of China stroke order. This learner path adapts those ten ordered medians to the vendored Noto Sans SC outline while preserving their order, their directions, the turns and nine intervening pen lifts; stroke widths and proportions differ between the Arphic-derived source graphics and Noto Sans SC.

source.citation: Hanzi Writer Data 道.json, ordered stroke paths and medians 1–12 (Hanzi Writer Data snapshot 68d10a4, updated from Make Me a Hanzi, 22 June 2019)
source.variation: The cited PRC-order dataset supplies twelve ordered strokes for 道, in two pieces, the walking piece written last. Medians 1–9 draw the upper right: a dot and a short left-falling stroke like two horns, a horizontal, then 自 as 自 is written alone. Medians 10–12 draw 辶 as 这 closes. Make Me a Hanzi documents that its stroke paths are ordered in proper stroke order, its medians use the same coordinate system for stroke-order animation, and the project follows People's Republic of China stroke order. This learner path adapts those twelve ordered medians to the vendored Noto Sans SC outline while preserving their order, their directions, the turns and eleven intervening pen lifts; stroke widths and proportions differ between the Arphic-derived source graphics and Noto Sans SC.

source.citation: Hanzi Writer Data 那.json, ordered stroke paths and medians 1–6 (Hanzi Writer Data snapshot 68d10a4, updated from Make Me a Hanzi, 22 June 2019)
source.variation: The cited PRC-order dataset supplies six ordered strokes for 那, in two pieces. Medians 1–4 draw the left piece: a horizontal that turns down the right side and hooks to the left at the foot without lifting, two horizontals, then a left-falling stroke from the top through both. Medians 5–6 draw 阝 on the right: a stroke that runs right, falls back to the left, swells round to the right and hooks to the left without lifting, then the vertical. Make Me a Hanzi documents that its stroke paths are ordered in proper stroke order, its medians use the same coordinate system for stroke-order animation, and the project follows People's Republic of China stroke order. This learner path adapts those six ordered medians to the vendored Noto Sans SC outline while preserving their order, their directions, the turns, the two hooks and five intervening pen lifts; stroke widths and proportions differ between the Arphic-derived source graphics and Noto Sans SC. Noto's left piece reaches lower than the source's, so its hook sits at the foot.

source.citation: Hanzi Writer Data 部.json, ordered stroke paths and medians 1–10 (Hanzi Writer Data snapshot 68d10a4, updated from Make Me a Hanzi, 22 June 2019)
source.variation: The cited PRC-order dataset supplies ten ordered strokes for 部, in two pieces. Medians 1–5 draw 立 as 意 opens: a dot, a horizontal, a short dot on the left, a short left-falling stroke on the right, then a long horizontal. Medians 6–8 draw 口 under it. Medians 9–10 draw the ear piece as 那 ends: a stroke that runs right, back to the left, round to the right and hooks to the left without lifting, then a long vertical. Make Me a Hanzi documents that its stroke paths are ordered in proper stroke order, its medians use the same coordinate system for stroke-order animation, and the project follows People's Republic of China stroke order. This learner path adapts those ten ordered medians to the vendored Noto Sans SC outline while preserving their order, their directions, the turns, the hook and nine intervening pen lifts; stroke widths and proportions differ between the Arphic-derived source graphics and Noto Sans SC.

source.citation: Hanzi Writer Data 都.json, ordered stroke paths and medians 1–10 (Hanzi Writer Data snapshot 68d10a4, updated from Make Me a Hanzi, 22 June 2019)
source.variation: The cited PRC-order dataset supplies ten ordered strokes for 都, in two pieces. Medians 1–8 draw 者 on the left: a short horizontal, the vertical through it, the long horizontal, a long left-falling stroke across them, then 日 under them as 日 is written alone. Medians 9–10 draw 阝 on the right as 那 closes: a stroke that runs right, falls back to the left, swells round to the right and hooks to the left without lifting, then the vertical. Make Me a Hanzi documents that its stroke paths are ordered in proper stroke order, its medians use the same coordinate system for stroke-order animation, and the project follows People's Republic of China stroke order. This learner path adapts those ten ordered medians to the vendored Noto Sans SC outline while preserving their order, their directions, the turns, the hook and nine intervening pen lifts; stroke widths and proportions differ between the Arphic-derived source graphics and Noto Sans SC.

source.citation: Hanzi Writer Data 酒.json, ordered stroke paths and medians 1–10 (Hanzi Writer Data snapshot 68d10a4, updated from Make Me a Hanzi, 22 June 2019)
source.variation: The cited PRC-order dataset supplies ten ordered strokes for 酒, in two pieces. Medians 1–3 draw the water piece as 洗 opens: two dots, then a rising stroke. Medians 4–10 draw the right side as 西 is written, with one stroke more: a horizontal, the box's left side, a horizontal that turns down the right side without lifting, a left-falling stroke and a vertical that bends right without lifting, both from above the box, a short horizontal across the inside, then the horizontal that closes the foot. Make Me a Hanzi documents that its stroke paths are ordered in proper stroke order, its medians use the same coordinate system for stroke-order animation, and the project follows People's Republic of China stroke order. This learner path adapts those ten ordered medians to the vendored Noto Sans SC outline while preserving their order, their directions, the turns and nine intervening pen lifts; stroke widths and proportions differ between the Arphic-derived source graphics and Noto Sans SC. Noto runs the box's right side straight down past the bottom horizontal, where the source's turns in to the left at the foot.

source.variation: The cited PRC-order dataset supplies seven ordered strokes for 里. Medians 1–4 draw the box of 田: its left side, the joined top and right side, the middle horizontal, the closing bottom; median 5 draws the vertical from the top of the box down through it; medians 6–7 draw the two horizontals of 土 on that vertical, the lower one longer. Make Me a Hanzi documents that its stroke paths are ordered in proper stroke order, its medians use the same coordinate system for stroke-order animation, and the project follows People's Republic of China stroke order. This learner path adapts those seven ordered medians to the vendored Noto Sans SC outline while preserving their order, their directions, the turn and six intervening pen lifts; stroke widths and proportions differ between the Arphic-derived source graphics and Noto Sans SC.

source.citation: Hanzi Writer Data 量.json, ordered stroke paths and medians 1–12 (Hanzi Writer Data snapshot 68d10a4, updated from Make Me a Hanzi, 22 June 2019)
source.variation: The cited PRC-order dataset supplies twelve ordered strokes for 量, in three pieces. Medians 1–4 draw 日 as 日 is written alone. Median 5 draws a long horizontal across the middle. Medians 6–12 draw 里 as 里 is written alone: its box (the left side, the top and right side, the middle horizontal, the bottom), a vertical down through the middle, a short horizontal, then a long horizontal along the foot. Make Me a Hanzi documents that its stroke paths are ordered in proper stroke order, its medians use the same coordinate system for stroke-order animation, and the project follows People's Republic of China stroke order. This learner path adapts those twelve ordered medians to the vendored Noto Sans SC outline while preserving their order, their directions, the turns and eleven intervening pen lifts; stroke widths and proportions differ between the Arphic-derived source graphics and Noto Sans SC.

source.citation: Hanzi Writer Data 钱.json, ordered stroke paths and medians 1–10 (Hanzi Writer Data snapshot 68d10a4, updated from Make Me a Hanzi, 22 June 2019)
source.variation: The cited PRC-order dataset supplies ten ordered strokes for 钱, in two pieces. Medians 1–5 draw the metal piece 钅 on the left: a left-falling stroke, two short horizontals, a short bar rising to the right, then a vertical that flicks up to the right at its foot without lifting. Medians 6–10 draw the right side: two short horizontals, a long slanting stroke that hooks up at its foot without lifting, a left-falling stroke across it, then a dot at the top right. Make Me a Hanzi documents that its stroke paths are ordered in proper stroke order, its medians use the same coordinate system for stroke-order animation, and the project follows People's Republic of China stroke order. This learner path adapts those ten ordered medians to the vendored Noto Sans SC outline while preserving their order, their directions, the turn, the hook and nine intervening pen lifts; stroke widths and proportions differ between the Arphic-derived source graphics and Noto Sans SC. Noto draws 钅's first stroke shorter than the source's and its fourth stroke level, where the source's rises to the right.

source.citation: Hanzi Writer Data 错.json, ordered stroke paths and medians 1–13 (Hanzi Writer Data snapshot 68d10a4, updated from Make Me a Hanzi, 22 June 2019)
source.variation: The cited PRC-order dataset supplies thirteen ordered strokes for 错, in two pieces. Medians 1–5 draw the metal piece as 钱 opens. Medians 6–13 draw the right side: a short horizontal, two short verticals through it, a long horizontal under them, then 日 in the order the standalone character uses. Make Me a Hanzi documents that its stroke paths are ordered in proper stroke order, its medians use the same coordinate system for stroke-order animation, and the project follows People's Republic of China stroke order. This learner path adapts those thirteen ordered medians to the vendored Noto Sans SC outline while preserving their order, their directions, the turns and twelve intervening pen lifts; stroke widths and proportions differ between the Arphic-derived source graphics and Noto Sans SC.

source.variation: The cited PRC-order dataset supplies ten ordered strokes for 难, in two pieces. Medians 1–2 draw 又 narrowed on the left: a horizontal that turns and falls to the left without lifting, then a dot instead of the long right-falling stroke. Medians 3–10 draw the right side as 准 ends: a left-falling stroke, a long vertical down the left, a dot at the top right, three short horizontals, a vertical through them, then a long horizontal at the foot. Make Me a Hanzi documents that its stroke paths are ordered in proper stroke order, its medians use the same coordinate system for stroke-order animation, and the project follows People's Republic of China stroke order. This learner path adapts those ten ordered medians to the vendored Noto Sans SC outline while preserving their order, their directions, the turn and nine intervening pen lifts; stroke widths and proportions differ between the Arphic-derived source graphics and Noto Sans SC.

source.citation: Hanzi Writer Data 雨.json, ordered stroke paths and medians 1–8 (Hanzi Writer Data snapshot 68d10a4, updated from Make Me a Hanzi, 22 June 2019)
source.variation: The cited PRC-order dataset supplies eight ordered strokes for 雨. Median 1 draws the top horizontal; medians 2–3 draw the frame, its left side, then a horizontal that turns down the right side and hooks to the left without lifting; median 4 draws the vertical down the middle; medians 5–8 draw the four dots, the two on the left first, upper then lower, then the two on the right. source.citation: Hanzi Writer Data 雪.json, ordered stroke paths and medians 1–11 (Hanzi Writer Data snapshot 68d10a4, updated from Make Me a Hanzi, 22 June 2019)
source.variation: The cited PRC-order dataset supplies eleven ordered strokes for 雪, in two pieces. Medians 1–8 draw 雨 on top, pressed flat, in the order 雨 alone uses: a short horizontal, a short stroke on the left, a horizontal that hooks down at its right end without lifting, the middle vertical, then the four dots, the left pair before the right. Medians 9–11 draw the lower piece: a horizontal that turns down its right side without lifting, then a horizontal across the middle and one along the foot. Make Me a Hanzi documents that its stroke paths are ordered in proper stroke order, its medians use the same coordinate system for stroke-order animation, and the project follows People's Republic of China stroke order. This learner path adapts those eleven ordered medians to the vendored Noto Sans SC outline while preserving their order, their directions, the turns and ten intervening pen lifts; stroke widths and proportions differ between the Arphic-derived source graphics and Noto Sans SC. Noto's cover turns straight down at its right end, and its four dots are short level dashes.

source.citation: Hanzi Writer Data 静.json, ordered stroke paths and medians 1–14 (Hanzi Writer Data snapshot 68d10a4, updated from Make Me a Hanzi, 22 June 2019)
source.variation: The cited PRC-order dataset supplies fourteen ordered strokes for 静, in two pieces. Medians 1–8 draw the left side as 情 ends: two horizontals, a vertical down through them, a long horizontal, then 月: a left side that curves to the lower left, a horizontal that turns down the right side and hooks to the left without lifting, and two short horizontals inside. Medians 9–14 draw the right side: a short left-falling stroke, a short horizontal that turns and falls to the left without lifting, a horizontal that turns down without lifting, a long horizontal through it, a horizontal under it, then a vertical down the middle that hooks to the left without lifting. Make Me a Hanzi documents that its stroke paths are ordered in proper stroke order, its medians use the same coordinate system for stroke-order animation, and the project follows People's Republic of China stroke order. This learner path adapts those fourteen ordered medians to the vendored Noto Sans SC outline while preserving their order, their directions, the turns, the hooks and thirteen intervening pen lifts; stroke widths and proportions differ between the Arphic-derived source graphics and Noto Sans SC. Noto runs the turned stroke on the right down past the long horizontal to the lower one.

source.citation: Hanzi Writer Data 面.json, ordered stroke paths and medians 1–9 (Hanzi Writer Data snapshot 68d10a4, updated from Make Me a Hanzi, 22 June 2019)
source.variation: The cited PRC-order dataset supplies nine ordered strokes for 面. Medians 1–2 draw a horizontal on top and a short left-falling stroke under its middle; medians 3–4 draw the frame: its left side, then a horizontal that turns down the right side without lifting; medians 5–8 draw the inside: two verticals, then two short horizontals between them; median 9 closes the frame along the bottom. Make Me a Hanzi documents that its stroke paths are ordered in proper stroke order, its medians use the same coordinate system for stroke-order animation, and the project follows People's Republic of China stroke order. This learner path adapts those nine ordered medians to the vendored Noto Sans SC outline while preserving their order, their directions, the turn and eight intervening pen lifts; stroke widths and proportions differ between the Arphic-derived source graphics and Noto Sans SC.

source.citation: Hanzi Writer Data 音.json, ordered stroke paths and medians 1–9 (Hanzi Writer Data snapshot 68d10a4, updated from Make Me a Hanzi, 22 June 2019)
source.variation: The cited PRC-order dataset supplies nine ordered strokes for 音, in two pieces. Medians 1–5 draw 立 on top: a dot, a horizontal, two short strokes leaning toward each other, then the long horizontal. Medians 6–9 draw 日 under it as 日 is written alone. Make Me a Hanzi documents that its stroke paths are ordered in proper stroke order, its medians use the same coordinate system for stroke-order animation, and the project follows People's Republic of China stroke order. This learner path adapts those nine ordered medians to the vendored Noto Sans SC outline while preserving their order, their directions, the turn and eight intervening pen lifts; stroke widths and proportions differ between the Arphic-derived source graphics and Noto Sans SC.

source.variation: The cited PRC-order dataset supplies fifteen ordered strokes for 题, in two pieces. Medians 1–9 draw 是 on the left: 日, a long horizontal, a short vertical with a short horizontal to its right, a left-falling stroke, then a long right-falling stroke along the foot. Medians 10–15 draw the page piece on the right: a horizontal, a short left-falling stroke, its left side, a horizontal that turns down the right side without lifting, a left-falling stroke inside, then a dot. Make Me a Hanzi documents that its stroke paths are ordered in proper stroke order, its medians use the same coordinate system for stroke-order animation, and the project follows People's Republic of China stroke order. This learner path adapts those fifteen ordered medians to the vendored Noto Sans SC outline while preserving their order, their directions, the turns and fourteen intervening pen lifts; stroke widths and proportions differ between the Arphic-derived source graphics and Noto Sans SC.

source.citation: Hanzi Writer Data 风.json, ordered stroke paths and medians 1–4 (Hanzi Writer Data snapshot 68d10a4, updated from Make Me a Hanzi, 22 June 2019)
source.variation: The cited PRC-order dataset supplies four ordered strokes for 风, in two pieces. Medians 1–2 draw the frame: a long left-falling stroke down the left side, then a horizontal that turns and slants down to the lower right, hooking up without lifting. Medians 3–4 draw inside it a short left-falling stroke and a dot crossing it. Make Me a Hanzi documents that its stroke paths are ordered in proper stroke order, its medians use the same coordinate system for stroke-order animation, and the project follows People's Republic of China stroke order. This learner path adapts those four ordered medians to the vendored Noto Sans SC outline while preserving their order, their directions, the turn, the hook and three intervening pen lifts; stroke widths and proportions differ between the Arphic-derived source graphics and Noto Sans SC.

lift, then draw the frame's top, turn down to the right and hook up
lift, then draw the inner left-falling stroke
lift, then draw the dot across it

source.citation: Hanzi Writer Data 饭.json, ordered stroke paths and medians 1–7 (Hanzi Writer Data snapshot 68d10a4, updated from Make Me a Hanzi, 22 June 2019)
source.variation: The cited PRC-order dataset supplies seven ordered strokes for 饭, in two pieces. Medians 1–3 draw the food piece 饣 on the left: a left-falling stroke, a short horizontal that hooks down to the left without lifting, then a vertical that flicks up to the right at its foot without lifting. Medians 4–7 draw 反 on the right: a flat left-falling stroke across the top, a long left-falling stroke down the left side, then 又 as 对 draws it, a horizontal that turns down to the left without lifting and the right-falling stroke. Make Me a Hanzi documents that its stroke paths are ordered in proper stroke order, its medians use the same coordinate system for stroke-order animation, and the project follows People's Republic of China stroke order. This learner path adapts those seven ordered medians to the vendored Noto Sans SC outline while preserving their order, their directions, the turns, the hook, the flick and six intervening pen lifts; stroke widths and proportions differ between the Arphic-derived source graphics and Noto Sans SC.

source.citation: Hanzi Writer Data 马.json, ordered stroke paths and medians 1–3 (Hanzi Writer Data snapshot 68d10a4, updated from Make Me a Hanzi, 22 June 2019)
source.variation: The cited PRC-order dataset supplies three ordered strokes for 马. Median 1 draws a horizontal that turns down without lifting; median 2 draws a long stroke that runs down, turns right, turns down again and hooks to the left without lifting; median 3 draws a rising stroke. These are the last three strokes of 吗 and 妈, in the same order. Make Me a Hanzi documents that its stroke paths are ordered in proper stroke order, its medians use the same coordinate system for stroke-order animation, and the project follows People's Republic of China stroke order. This learner path adapts those three ordered medians to the vendored Noto Sans SC outline while preserving their order, their directions, the turns, the hook and two intervening pen lifts; stroke widths and proportions differ between the Arphic-derived source graphics and Noto Sans SC.

lift, then draw the long stroke down, right, down and hook left
lift, then draw the rising horizontal

source.citation: Hanzi Writer Data 高.json, ordered stroke paths and medians 1–10 (Hanzi Writer Data snapshot 68d10a4, updated from Make Me a Hanzi, 22 June 2019)
source.variation: The cited PRC-order dataset supplies ten ordered strokes for 高, in three pieces. Medians 1–2 draw a dot and a long horizontal on top. Medians 3–5 draw 口 in the order the standalone character uses. Medians 6–10 draw the foot: the frame's left side, a horizontal that turns down the right side and hooks to the left without lifting, then a small 口 inside it, again in the order the standalone character uses. Make Me a Hanzi documents that its stroke paths are ordered in proper stroke order, its medians use the same coordinate system for stroke-order animation, and the project follows People's Republic of China stroke order. This learner path adapts those ten ordered medians to the vendored Noto Sans SC outline while preserving their order, their directions, the turns, the hook and nine intervening pen lifts; stroke widths and proportions differ between the Arphic-derived source graphics and Noto Sans SC.

source.citation: Hanzi Writer Data 鬼.json, ordered stroke paths and medians 1–9 (Hanzi Writer Data snapshot 68d10a4, updated from Make Me a Hanzi, 22 June 2019)
source.variation: The cited PRC-order dataset supplies nine ordered strokes for 鬼, in three pieces. Medians 1–5 draw 白 on top as 白 is written alone. Medians 6–7 draw the legs: a long left-falling stroke from inside 白, then a vertical that bends right along the foot and hooks up without lifting. Medians 8–9 draw 厶 inside the bend as 去 ends: a stroke that falls to the left and turns right without lifting, then a dot. Make Me a Hanzi documents that its stroke paths are ordered in proper stroke order, its medians use the same coordinate system for stroke-order animation, and the project follows People's Republic of China stroke order. This learner path adapts those nine ordered medians to the vendored Noto Sans SC outline while preserving their order, their directions, the turns, the hook and eight intervening pen lifts; stroke widths and proportions differ between the Arphic-derived source graphics and Noto Sans SC.
